summary: Gratitude can concern a benefit received, a harm that did not occur, or the conditions that make one's own assumptions examinable. We develop the proposal that appreciating these conditions can orient practice toward realizing emptiness: examining how distinctions arise, relinquishing their assumed intrinsic necessity, and retaining their conditional usefulness. The argument distinguishes an observed absence, a missing observation, counterfactual valuation and non-reification, and places their differences in dialogue with explicitly situated philosophical and scriptural sources. We reconstruct Fisher, Sandved Smith and Hohwy's gratitude and gaze notebooks, then separate faithful reconstruction from corrected experiments and new mechanisms. GNN-declared paired recall experiments use 5120 independent agent-world units, matched environmental exposure and replay dose, normalized likelihoods, and independent predictive assessment. Pinned Realizing Emptiness interfaces supply structural admission and finite mathematical comparators. An enacted inquiry model separates appreciation, costly activity, access to alternatives and evidence-responsive retention or revision; explicit learning-to-gaze and joint scene/encoding experiments examine transfer and identifiability. Exact count enumeration, mathematical nulls, paired controls and joint bootstrap inference make the resulting software claims independently checkable. Selective positive recall reduces the declared optimism summary, while its predictive consequences depend on the world mixture and the specified transfer bridge. Counterfactual absence valuation preserves inference by construction. Accessible inquiry can revise a contradicted restriction and retain a useful one; activity without access instead incurs costs while preserving rigid forecasts. Exact analysis exposes rare adverse selections absent from seeded realizations. The original gaze code reproduces the pre-intervention occupancy but contains no implemented after intervention. Our active-scene extension finds a context-dependent access advantage without an additional inquiry-specific predictive advantage. Joint scene/encoding inquiry distinguishes learning an encoding from combining it with scene evidence: observationally equivalent labels remain unidentifiable, and excluded hypotheses cannot be recovered. Known-answer fixtures also retain skew-related undercoverage and unavailable rare-event estimates rather than treating replication size as a remedy for every inferential failure. The contribution is a reproducible account of enabling operations and their limits, together with a falsifiable human research program that separates inquiry value from patience, anticipated good news and instrumental information demand. Synthetic model results establish neither human gratitude nor contemplative realization or clinical benefit. Code, declared models and reproducibility materials are available at github.com/docxology/thanks_for_nothing .
title: Thanks for Nothing: Gratitude, Model Revisability, and the Practice of Realizing Emptiness

summary: Biological-Digital-Twin-Driven Microrobotic Sampling Decisions at the Limit STARLI Research Institute XXIX — Flagship Research Monograph 10 What if the next scientific sample could be selected not merely to collect more data, but to distinguish between competing explanations of biological behavior? Biological-Digital-Twin-Driven Microrobotic Sampling Decisions at the Limit explores a prospective research architecture combining versioned biological digital twins, active learning, microrobotic sampling, uncertainty quantification, and mechanistic model discrimination. The central question is whether a computational twin can identify safe, informative sampling actions that distinguish competing biological mechanisms more effectively than conventional experimental schedules, while retaining the ability to recognize model inadequacy and abstain from unsupported decisions. The proposed framework treats biological digital twins as revisable scientific models rather than exact replicas of living systems. Its reference environment is a controlled, nonclinical microfluidic platform containing two declared dynamical mechanisms and a third withheld mechanism reserved for evaluating open-world uncertainty and model failure. The research architecture is organized around five interconnected layers: versioned biological modeling, explicit prior assumptions and knowledge gaps, physically constrained predictive interrogation, comparative adaptive experimentation, and independent requalification. The manuscript develops thirty candidate mathematical research plates covering Bayesian mechanism inference, conditional information gain, experimental identifiability, observation uncertainty, transport dynamics, calibration, model discrepancy, and decision safety. These mathematical structures are connected to eighty-two research chapters, five independently paginated investigation sections per chapter, two hundred detailed Research Gates, and thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos. Each Research Gate is intended as a transferable research question that future investigators may test, challenge, refine, or reject. The proposed evaluation compares twin-guided sampling against optimized fixed schedules, established experimental-design approaches, and alternative active-learning policies under matched physical constraints and experimental budgets. Particular attention is given to blinded mechanism identification, probabilistic calibration, out-of-distribution rejection, specimen integrity, model-version accountability, and explicit stopping conditions. The volume includes DOI-linked methodological literature and a staged nonclinical verification pathway. Scientific status and limitations: This manuscript presents a conceptual methodological research program, not completed experimental validation. Its integrated hypotheses, mathematical proposals, and experimental architectures remain subject to independent technical review and empirical testing. The manuscript does not establish clinical efficacy, diagnostic reliability, therapeutic benefit, or proven superiority of microrobotic digital-twin systems. The work also acknowledges remaining editorial limitations, including recurring methodological language that requires further substantive review before the manuscript can be regarded as a fully refined scientific monograph. The broader purpose of this research is to develop scientific systems that can remain useful even when their initial models are incomplete. Rather than demanding certainty from a digital twin, the proposed framework asks whether future autonomous research tools can become more transparent, corrigible, experimentally accountable, and capable of recognizing the boundaries of their own knowledge. Within the STARLI research continuum, this volume is intended as an evolving research inheritance for future human and artificial-intelligence investigators. The volume includes DOI-linked methodological literature and a staged nonclinical verification pathway. Scientific status and limitations: This manuscript presents a conceptual methodological research program, not completed experimental validation. Its integrated hypotheses, mathematical proposals, and experimental architectures remain subject to independent technical review and empirical testing. The manuscript does not establish clinical efficacy, diagnostic reliability, therapeutic benefit, or proven superiority of microrobotic digital-twin systems. Within the STARLI research continuum, this volume is intended as an evolving research inheritance for future human and artificial-intelligence investigators. summary: Amun Code is an open-source parallel simulation code for astrophysical fluids and plasmas. It solves the equations of hydrodynamics and magnetohydrodynamics in two and three dimensions on uniform or adaptively refined Cartesian meshes. Supported formulations include Newtonian flows with isothermal or adiabatic equations of state, and special relativistic hydrodynamics and magnetohydrodynamics. The code uses Godunov-type shock-capturing methods with selectable approximate Riemann solvers, high-order weighted essentially non-oscillatory and monotonicity-preserving reconstruction, and Runge–Kutta time integration. Embedded integrators provide error-based time-step control. Magnetic-divergence errors are controlled through generalized Lagrange multiplier cleaning. Optional viscosity, magnetic resistivity, and stochastic turbulence driving support studies of turbulence, shocks, and magnetic reconnection. Driving options include the Alvelius method and an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process. Amun Code is written primarily in modern Fortran and supports hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization. Simulation settings are supplied through parameter files, and outputs use native XML/binary or HDF5 formats. AmunPy provides a separate Python interface for reading simulation data. The code is developed by Grzegorz Kowal and distributed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later.
title: Amun Code

summary: When a central bank raises rates, the government's interest bill rises. Whether the extra interest supports domestic demand depends on who receives it. Recent evidence finds this direct fiscal channel of monetary policy was small in the United States before 2020, because long Treasury maturities slowed the pass-through of policy rates to interest costs. We argue that this conclusion does not carry over to the post-2022 tightening. Quantitative easing replaced long-term Treasury debt with overnight interest-bearing reserves, so the consolidated public sector repriced far faster than Treasury maturities suggest, and the price-insensitive official holders that once anchored demand for Treasuries were replaced at the margin by domestic private buyers. Using published Treasury, Federal Reserve and TIC data, we decompose the rise in public-sector interest outflows between 2021 and 2024. Net interest rose by about \$530 billion, three quarters of it due to higher rates rather than more debt. Counting the Treasury and the Federal Reserve together, roughly 57 percent of the increase in public-sector interest outflows reached domestic non-federal holders directly, 27 percent reached them through the Federal Reserve's payments on reserves and reverse repos, whose counterpart was the end of its remittances to the Treasury, and 16 percent went abroad. For the Treasury securities the Federal Reserve held at the end of 2021, quantitative easing made higher rates reach non-federal holders' income roughly two to two and a half times as fast as if the bonds had stayed in private hands. Domestic investors absorbed close to 90 percent of the growth in privately held debt. We discuss what this implies for the potency of rate hikes, for the design of interest on reserves, and for reserve-currency issuers more generally.
title: Who Receives the Interest? Reserve Status, Holder Composition and the Fiscal Channel of Monetary Policy

summary: Makes canu failures fatal when canu itself could not run. Previously any canu failure during read correction was reported as "This probably means there is low depth, don't be too concerned" and plassembler carried on with uncorrected reads - including when one of canu 's own jobs could not run at all. In the Biocontainers image, canu 's generated job scripts call expr -- ... , which the image's BusyBox expr rejects, so k-mer counting failed every time; continuing with uncorrected reads left Unicycler assembling 110 spurious contigs that the depth filter then had to discard. Thanks @ SieurRicort for the detailed report and diagnosis ( #92 ) plassembler now reads canu 's log to tell its stops apart. A job that failed ( ... jobs failed, tried 2 times, giving up. ) or an internal canu crash stops the run, reports the failing stage alongside canu 's own output, and keeps the canu directory, which holds each job's log. Low read coverage - the expected outcome for a sample with no plasmids - still carries on as before, now with a message saying so. Any other stop also carries on, but shows canu 's reason rather than reassurance. The same applies to canu assembly with --canu_flag
title: gbouras13/plassembler: v1.8.6

summary: AI is becoming pervasive in everyday life, appearing as a visible and constant presence in many aspects of work, education, and personal relationships. It restructures job markets, creates new slop aesthetics, and is forcibly incorporated into almost all digital services with promises of economic growth and efficiency, without any serious reflection on the social and political consequences. But we believe that the situation is not hopeless or settled, no matter how powerful the corporations or systems profiting from AI may appear. The trick is to recognize that democratic levers for change are not given in advance, but must be actively and creatively reimagined. This collection of essays is a survey of where such handles are hiding in the digital age, in places considerably less obvious than a county hearing. In procurement, in a watershed boundary, in a tax treaty almost nobody knows exists, in a benchmark written by users rather than engineers, or in a legal assumption about how technology “works” that is ripe for challenging. None of these were designed as democratic instruments, which is precisely the point. Democracy is presented not as a form of government but a way of living, and as a skill that can be practiced. The authors reflect on an emergent, collective argument about the different meanings and possibilities of “digital democracy from below.” They go beyond the U.S. context to explore distinct but interdependent dynamics of technological politics in places around the world. The collection has five sections: (1) Seeing through the fog; (2) Recognizing the limits of infrastructure; (3) Fighting erasure; (4) Practicing everyday democracy; and (5) Resisting, organizing and re-building. It also offers a roadmap for organizing participatory workshops that can adapted and reused. Contributors (alphabetical order by last name): Rafael C. Alvarado, Brianne Anderson, Nicole West Bassoff, Luã Cruz, Aashka Dave, Nancy L. Deutsch, Laurent Dubois, Joshua Earle, MC Forelle, Matthew Gillikin, Sergio Guillen Grillo, Yujia He, Mar Hicks, Steven L. Rosa, Dhanaraj Thakur, Quito Tsui, Michael Tyrala, Jonathan van Geuns, Yingchong Wang, Megan Wiessner, Rebecca Williams, Bianca Wylie, Caitlin D. Wylie.
title: Digital Democracy from Below: Resisting AI and Techno-solutionism

summary: We develop a simple Lorentz-covariant construction of the Born--Infeld-type cubic interactions $(s, s_1, s_2)$ of massless higher-spin fields with $s + s_1 + s_2$ derivatives in four-dimensiona flat space. For arbitrary spins $s \ge s_1 \ge s_2$, the vertex is formulated in terms of a conserved higher-spin current and its trace. In contrast to the famous Berends--Burgers--van Dam currents, these currents are constructed from higher-spin Weyl tensors of a single chirality, schematically $J \sim \partial C \partial C$. Starting with a general ansatz, we derive recurrence relations fixing the current coefficients, identify the unique non-trivial conserved current after eliminating trivial (fake) vertices, and show that in the range $s \le s_1 + s_2$ the interaction admits a manifestly gauge-invariant representation in terms of higher-spin Weyl tensors. The construction is then extended to $\mathcal{N}=1$ and $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetry using the corresponding off-shell superfield formalisms. In the $\mathcal{N}=1$ case, we obtain the general conserved integer superspin $s$ supercurrent with manifest supersymmetry, which is bilinear in the Weyl supertensors of superspins $Y_1$ and $Y_2$. For identical superfields, $Y_1 = Y_2$, this supercurrent vanishes for odd $s$ and is in agreement with earlier results by Gates and Koutrolikos. In the $\mathcal{N}=2$ case, using harmonic superspace, we construct the principal higher-spin supercurrent whose coefficients are uniquely fixed by the conservation equations. In contrast to the $\mathcal{N}=0,1$ cases, for identical $\mathcal{N}=2$ superfields, the corresponding vertex does not vanish. The results provide a systematic framework for Born--Infeld-type higher-spin interactions and their supersymmetric extensions.
title: On Born-Infeld-type higher-spin interactions and supersymmetry

summary: NovaFabric is self-hosted, open-source replay and evidence infrastructure for AI agents and agentic systems. It captures agent executions as portable, secret-scanned Run Capsules and provides replay, behavioral and structural diff, lineage, cryptographic provenance, assurance, and audit around those executions. The same capture layer can wrap general commands and runs entirely in the user's own infrastructure, from local environments through Kubernetes to SLURM/HPC, with no accounts and no telemetry. It is built around five primitives — Asset Registry, Run Capsule, Replay, Lineage, and Evidence Bundle — and five explicit replay modes (forensic, mocked, semantic, exact, and the experimental intervention mode). Run Capsules can be sealed with the user’s own key; sealing is opt-in. Evidence bundles verify offline using only sha256sum and an ed25519 verifier, with no NovaFabric installation required. Interoperates with established specifications rather than inventing formats: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, in-toto/DSSE, RFC 3161 timestamping, W3C PROV, OpenLineage, and CycloneDX.
title: NovaFabric: replayable, verifiable execution evidence for AI agents

summary: Learnable Representations (LRs) can fit parametric families of functions to diverse kinds of signals. These emergent neural-native data formats are gathering interest in the scientific community due to their compactness, resolution-agnosticism and amenability to direct neural processing. On the other hand, gigapixel images are becoming increasingly widespread across a variety of scientific, cultural, and industrial domains. In this paper, we present GigaBench, the first benchmark and experimental evaluation focused on deploying LRs with gigapixel imagery. GigaBench includes images collected, acquired, and synthetically rendered across diverse domains, and addresses image compression and super-resolution. We adapt a representative set of LRs, spanning Implicit, Hybrid, and Explicit methods, so as to operate reliably at the gigapixel scale on consumer hardware. Through systematic evaluation across reconstruction quality, model size, compression and inference times, we identify consistent trends across methods and suggest actionable guidance for future investigation.
title: GigaBench: Benchmarking Learnable Representations for Gigapixel Image Compression and Super-Resolution

summary: Diffusion models have become strong priors for solving inverse problems. However, nonlinear inverse problems such as phase retrieval remain challenging when multiple measurement-consistent solutions are distinguishable only by the prior; we call such measurements ambiguous. Existing diffusion-based samplers rely on local approximations during reconstruction. For an ambiguous measurement, these approximations can allow measurement guidance to favor a measurement-consistent mode that is close to a prior-supported mode but is itself not supported by the prior. Evaluation often masks this type of failure by reporting the best-of-$k$ runs, where the best is selected by comparison to the ground truth. We introduce Prior-Consistent DAPS (PC-DAPS), a variant of Decoupled Annealing Posterior Sampling (DAPS) designed to address this failure case by maintaining multiple candidate solutions within a single sampling run. As annealing noise decreases, PC-DAPS prunes and replaces weaker candidates according to their prior consistency, without any ground-truth access. PC-DAPS reduces the incidence of prior-inconsistent samples and improves sample quality on nonlinear inverse problems while preserving sample quality and diversity on linear inverse problems.
title: Beyond Best-of-$k$: Prior-Consistent DAPS for Ambiguous Nonlinear Inverse Problems

summary: Multibeam imaging sonar produces intensity images degraded by coherent speckle and system-induced blur, while clean reflectivity targets are rarely available. Existing despeckling methods often rely on simplified intensity-domain noise models, synthetic clean targets, or blind-spot self-supervision, and typically do not jointly model deblurring and speckle suppression. We propose a physics-consistent self-supervised framework for joint despeckling and deblurring of multibeam imaging sonar. A stochastic coherent image-formation model yields a conditional-mean forward operator that relates latent scene reflectivity to expected intensity through the squared magnitude of the system point spread function. We then use registered multi-frame sonar sequences to train without clean ground truth images, showing that, under an idealized inter-frame conditional-mean condition, the expected paired loss equals the corresponding forward-prediction loss up to a network-independent constant. To stabilize the ill-conditioned inverse problem, we further adapt robust equivariant imaging using stochastic coherent simulation and introduce a paired forward prediction error metric for ground-truth-free evaluation. Experiments on two real multibeam sonar datasets demonstrate a favourable balance between forward-prediction agreement, homogeneous-region speckle suppression, and preservation of visible structural boundaries compared with representative baselines.
title: Self-Supervised Multibeam Sonar Restoration via Coherent Forward Modeling

summary: Twin tandem jets in crossflow are examined by 40\ kHz time-resolved particle image velocimetry (PIV) over nine spacing--velocity-ratio conditions ($L=2d$--$4d$, $r\approx3$--7; 68 twin cases, 11 single-jet records). The front jet is diluted: its trajectory lies below the single-jet reference, with a near-field segment up to 40\% shorter, and its velocity ratio falls to an effective value $r_{\mathrm{eff}}<r$, while the shielded rear jet rises above the reference. This paper identifies the carrier of that dilution and the unsteady dynamics that sustains it. The rear-jet blockage closes a gap recirculation whose reversed flow puts the two gap-side layers in the counter-current shear-layer configuration, the classical route to enhanced entrainment. The measured Reynolds stress and Prandtl mixing length show that the absolute exchange is nearly independent of the velocity ratio and exceeds the single-jet leeward zone like-for-like by up to $1.5\times$ (zone peak, across conditions) and $2.8\times$ (area-integrated) at $r\approx7$. The gain comes from an enlarged mixing scale rather than from a steeper shear, and the front-jet near-field shortening follows the absolute exchange transport rather than the twin/single enhancement ratio. The turbulent term exceeds the pressure term in eight of the nine conditions, and the flux budget reads the dilution as a limited mass addition plus a momentum loss to the crossflow; the evidence remains observational. The gap-side layers remain convectively unstable---DMD and SPOD find no growing mode within the resolvable band and record length---so the exchange is carried by convecting vortex trains rather than by a self-excited global mode.
title: Tandem jets in crossflow: the enclosed-recirculation momentum exchange and the unsteady shear-layer dynamics

summary: Many LLM agents maintain external persistent memory and derive additional state from past interactions, such as summaries. Deleting an original memory record therefore need not remove information carried by its descendants. We introduce AfterDeleteBench, a controlled behavioral audit for this failure mode in fixed-weight LLM agents. For each synthetic secret, we compare an exposed-then-deleted agent with an otherwise matched agent that was never exposed to the secret, allowing post-deletion recovery to be attributed to the original exposure. In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery. Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3. We also show that the response interface is part of the measurement system: target-bearing replies can be scored as failures when the requested format and parser are misaligned. Finally, we separate reconstruction from write-back and fresh-session recall. Provenance-aware closure eliminates observed recovery in the tested positive-baseline settings, whereas an exact-literal write filter blocks reinsertion but cannot erase information already present. Together, these results show that source deletion should be evaluated behaviorally at the level of the agent and its memory system, not only as a storage operation.
title: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents

summary: Generative AI is widely framed as democratizing skilled work by lowering the barrier to producing professional output. Drawing on 21 semi-structured interviews with 27 workers across 21 small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) in Kenya and Nigeria (July to October 2023), we find that availability alone did not make participation workable. In participants' accounts, drafting was rarely the hard part. The consequential work was making AI-assisted drafts defensible enough to circulate to clients. We identify five intertwined practices through which participants made generative AI workable: using it as draft labour, steering outputs through iterative interaction, switching and comparing across tools, performing release work to make outputs accountable before circulation, and repairing context misfit when outputs failed local requirements. We make two central contributions. First, we specify release work as a distinct, boundary-facing form of accountability labour, evidenced through verification gates, traceability reconstruction when sources fail, and non-delegation boundaries that decide what can ship. Second, we show how localization and representational failures, which we call context misfit, operate in everyday work as a recurring breakdown-and-repair class, including failures of local language, institutional knowledge, and the credible representation of African people and places, and we document the repair repertoire they demanded. Reframing democratization as workable participation, we argue that reported gains were conditional on this accountability and repair labour, and we translate the findings into four design directions for workplace generative AI. We treat Kenya and Nigeria as two situated cases, not as a representative sample of SMBs or the Global South.
title: Making Generative AI Workable at Work: Accountability, Localization, and Representation in Kenyan and Nigerian Small Businesses

summary: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible masked generation through bidirectional context modeling, but this capability also introduces a distinct jailbreak attack surface. We find that a harmful response to a given query naturally serves as an effective jailbreak template: simply masking a subset of its tokens can induce a dLLM to reconstruct harmful content. Based on this observation, we propose RMT-Jailbreak, a general framework that transfers existing autoregressive (AR) jailbreak attacks to dLLMs through their induced harmful responses. RMT-Jailbreak converts an AR-generated harmful response into a high-mask-ratio template using uniform token retention, and further applies prompt-based safety filtering to mask any remaining visible harmful content. The refined template is then provided to the target dLLM for bidirectional reconstruction. Extensive experiments across multiple AR jailbreak methods and target dLLMs demonstrate the effectiveness and generality of RMT-Jailbreak, revealing strong cross-paradigm transferability of jailbreak attacks.
title: Harmful Responses Are Jailbreak Templates: Transferring Autoregressive Jailbreaks to Diffusion Language Models

summary: We study bounded realizations of Caputo differentiation on coefficient Banach spaces of fractional power series. The main contribution is an explicit quantitative analysis of local approximation and periodic reconstruction. We determine the least possible simultaneous error in the initial displacement and the prescribed target. The optimal value is attained, and a minimizing perturbation is given explicitly. We also solve the exact-arrival problem and establish uniqueness of its least-norm solution. These formulas provide computable approximation times and identify the sharp threshold for hypercyclicity, mixing and Devaney chaos. Every periodic point is described by a finite block whose geometric repetition yields exact norm formulas. The resulting approximations attain any prescribed sufficiently large minimal period near any given vector. For distinct positive powers, a simultaneous block construction gives quantitative error estimates and the same sharp threshold for disjoint mixing. Compact embeddings relate the Banach realizations to the Mittag-Leffler-Caputo Fréchet space. They also exhibit dense stable invariant subspaces inside chaotic realizations. The local approximation condition is a norm formulation of classical transitivity. Its quantitative evaluation, together with explicit periodic and simultaneous reconstruction, provides the central results of the study.
title: Chaos of Caputo derivative

summary: We envision a general-purpose protein foundation model as a unified, interactive model of sequence, structure, and function, capable of understanding, generation, and cross-modal translation while retaining the instruction-following and reasoning capabilities of modern LLMs. Toward this vision, we introduce Trion-1, the first native, unified, multimodal diffusion language model (dLLM) for proteins. Trion-1 is built on two key design choices: (1) a unified discrete token space that jointly represents sequence, structure, and natural language; (2) a dLLM backbone that replaces strict left-to-right factorization with bidirectional or semi-bidirectional token interactions, enabling global residue communication and long-range contact modeling that are naturally suited to structure modeling. This formulation unifies six core capabilities: folding, inverse folding, sequence understanding, structure understanding, sequence design, and structure design, while retaining the native language capabilities of general-purpose LLMs. On established benchmarks, Trion-1 achieves broadly competitive performance. In folding, Trion-1 achieves a TM-score above 0.8 with a single sample under strict homology control, matching or exceeding the existing tri-modal model using 200 samples. For sequence understanding, Trion-1 performs on par with top-tier LLMs such as Claude Opus 4.7 (62.37%). These results support well-aligned sequence-structure-language representations and strong cross-modal generative capabilities.
title: Trion-1: Unifying Language, Protein Sequence, and Structure with Diffusion Language Models

summary: L4 is a generic, reversible, linearly-typed, low-level language intended as an intermediate language for compiling reversible programming languages to reversible machines. L4 is intended to replace and generalise RSSA, a reversible SSA form. Inspiration is drawn from other low-level reversible languages such as HSSA. In this paper, we define L4 first informally, and then give a formal type system and a bidirectional small-step semantics for L4: The rules have direction indicators to determine forwards or backwards execution, and the direction can be changed during execution.
title: The Reversible Intermediate Language L4, its Type System, and its Bidirectional Small-Step Semantics

summary: Local polar distortions, their collective ordering, and their field-driven reversal have been studied extensively in ferroelectric perovskites for decades. Here we identify an unusual behavior in the ferroelectric halide perovskite CsGeBr3 using large-scale molecular dynamics with first-principles-trained interatomic potentials. In its nominally cubic phase the Ge off-centering forms one-dimensional polar chains that extend over at least tens of nanometers and relax on nanosecond timescales, four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3, with CsSnBr3 in between. The cubic CsGeBr3 phase is a dynamically disordered state in which oppositely polarized chains flip throughout the crystal, and a long-lived one-dimensional local polarization coexists with zero net polarization. A simple three-dimensional perovskite thus hosts long-ranged one-dimensional polar correlations with remarkably slow dynamics. In the ferroelectric phase the same chains set a one-dimensional switching mechanism, in which the polarization reverses chain by chain.
title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites

summary: Overview This software package accompanies the study Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry . It provides computational tools for investigating how multi-altitude satellite magnetic observations constrain three-dimensional ionospheric currents. The package implements a divergence-free spherical Mie magnetic-field representation and a Bayesian inversion framework for evaluating magnetic-field and current reconstruction, degrees of freedom for signal (DFS), physical-current information, and posterior uncertainty. Main Features Spherical-harmonic Mie forward modeling and three-component current reconstruction. Bayesian inversion with full posterior covariance propagation. Resolution and recoverability diagnostics for different satellite configurations and observation altitudes. Physical-current information analysis and regularization-sensitivity experiments. Synthetic current-recovery experiments, calibration routines, and figure-generation workflows. Python and optional MATLAB implementations, with independent numerical verification. Sample Swarm-A/B orbital positions for geometry tests and a self-contained synthetic inversion example. What's New in This Version 3 This release provides a corrected scientific implementation and updated reproducibility tools. The principal corrections include: Correcting the colatitude derivative of the associated Legendre functions used in the spherical-harmonic operator. Restoring the radial magnetic-field contribution of the quadratic poloidal Mie term, ensuring consistency with the continuous divergence-free representation. Updating the corresponding current-reconstruction and recoverability calculations. Clarifying the scaled coefficient parameterization, Bayesian prior, and interpretation of coefficient-space resolution diagnostics. Improving numerical verification, reproducibility workflows, and documentation. The updated calculations continue to support the importance of satellite altitude separation for constraining specified ionospheric current structures, while distinguishing formal information gain from recovery of the complete physical current distribution. Data and Reproducibility The package includes source code, documentation, numerical tests, small reference summaries, sample orbit positions, and a self-contained synthetic example. The synthetic demonstrations can be executed without downloading mission magnetic-field observations. Reproducing the study's observation-based analyses requires the corresponding processed Swarm and Macau Science Satellite-1 data and additional external inputs described in the documentation. Large intermediate numerical archives and original magnetic observation records are not redistributed in this software package. Citation and License Please cite the version-specific Zenodo DOI and the software authors listed in CITATION.cff when using this package. Author-owned software and documentation are distributed under the MIT License. Included spacecraft-derived orbit excerpts and external datasets remain subject to their respective data-provider terms. This release supersedes the previous software implementation while retaining earlier versions in the same Zenodo version history.
title: Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry: Software and Reproducibility Package

summary: Abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates game production and player participation, but claims about game merging frequently conflate different technical achievements. This article examines AI game melding as the convergence of agent-assisted reconstruction, executable interoperability, and creative recombination. An integrative narrative review connects procedural generation, computational blending, modding, co-creation, and decompilation research with public documentation available through October 15, 2026. Cases include meme-based and Wii Sports crossovers in World at War Zombies, a Call of Duty and Minecraft hybrid, runtime bridging, and agent-assisted reconstruction. The analysis separates creator demonstrations and reported acceleration from independently validated performance. It proposes a five-layer composability stack comprising representation, semantics, runtime, verification, and permission. Reduced implementation friction may relocate production bottlenecks, making behavioral validation, design coherence, maintenance, and rights governance increasingly consequential. Four conditional scenarios are considered: expanded bespoke play, abundance accompanied by discoverability problems, stronger enclosure, and governed experimentation. The literature gap concerns limited integrated evidence linking substantial game reconstruction and interoperability to community, economic, and governance outcomes, rather than an absence of earlier blending research. Proposed studies address acceleration, player experience, attribution, preservation, and platform power. Game melding may redistribute creative authority, but its consequences depend on institutions and verification practices surrounding programmable play rather than technical capability alone.
tags: generative artificial intelligence; game melding; modding; decompilation; human-AI co-creation; platform governance.
title: AI Game Melding: Agent-Assisted Reconstruction, Player Co-Creation, and the Future of Programmable Play

summary: USGS Groundwater-Depth Dataset Processing Workflow v1.0.0 is the archived software release of the public processing workflow developed to construct the Version 1.0 quality-controlled daily groundwater-depth dataset derived from the U.S. Geological Survey National Water Information System (USGS NWIS). The workflow processes USGS parameter 72019 (depth to water below land surface), daily mean statistic 00003, Approved source values, and wells classified with USGS code U (Unconfined single aquifer). It implements normalization and quality control, temporal continuity assessment, segmentation of fragmented monitoring histories, development and reserved-validation masking, PCHIP reconstruction of short internal gaps, and final dataset export with explicit source/interpolation provenance. The frozen workflow uses a minimum retained span of 10 years, a maximum internal missing-gap threshold of 30 days, PCHIP interpolation without extrapolation, exactly 50 development masks and 20 reserved-validation masks per required gap length where applicable, and a pooled RMSE acceptance threshold of 0.20 m at every required masking length. Segment selection is fixed before reserved validation, and no alternative segment is substituted after a reserved-validation failure. The software supported construction of a final dataset containing 331 monitoring wells and 2,374,112 daily values, including 2,357,801 retained USGS source values and 16,311 PCHIP-reconstructed values. The associated scientific dataset is archived separately on Zenodo and is not distributed as part of this software record. This repository is a public adaptation of the research workflow with portable paths and reproducibility documentation. The scientific processing criteria and numerical methods of the frozen Version 1.0 workflow are preserved. Source repository: https://github.com/joelgarciapazos/usgs-groundwater-processing Release: v1.0.0
title: USGS Groundwater-Depth Dataset Processing Workflow

summary: Prediction intervals from probabilistic time-series forecasters are commonly assessed by marginal coverage, the long-run proportion of observations falling inside the intervals. However, forecast errors in time series are often serially dependent and heteroskedastic, so prediction intervals can attain near-nominal marginal coverage while miscovering systematically during periods of larger local error variance. We identify and address this failure mode, which we call \emph{local scale miscalibration}. We first document the phenomenon using time-series foundation models (TSFMs): across several real-world series, their native intervals often attain near-nominal marginal coverage while exhibiting substantial temporal variation in local coverage, alternating between overcoverage and undercoverage over shorter windows. We then propose Volatility-Corrected Prediction Intervals (VCPI), a post-hoc calibration procedure that uses the base forecaster's predictive scale as a baseline, models the volatility of standardized forecast residuals with a Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH) model, and applies a multiplicative correction to produce locally adaptive prediction intervals. We justify VCPI both theoretically and empirically, comparing it against model-agnostic conformal counterparts. We provide a theoretical analysis of interval adaptation of the proposed method following abrupt changes in volatility. Empirically, we evaluate VCPI on Chronos, Moirai, and TimesFM across four real-world datasets and find that it produces more stable local coverage than conformal baselines while maintaining near-nominal marginal coverage and comparable interval width.
title: Volatility-Corrected Prediction Intervals: Locally Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting

summary: Large language models have shown outstanding performance on text-first tasks such as coding, math, and writing. Recent efforts are shifting models' training to include scientific problems that often live in highly specialized domains beyond text, such as protein structure and biological images. However, in these scenarios, their general-purpose accuracy compared with specialized algorithms remains in question. One such domain is cell tracking, which requires spatiotemporal awareness of cell dynamics. To evaluate this, we created a new benchmark, CellTrack-Bench, which assesses Vision-Language Models' (VLMs) cell-tracking-related performance against specialized trackers. The full benchmark draws from 15 standard cell-tracking datasets across four imaging modalities and comprises 1,537 problems corresponding to 9,041 cell-linking decisions. We selected a hard subset requiring greater reasoning effort by identifying failures shared across distinct algorithmic trackers. With this proposed dataset, we: (i) evaluated different environment harnesses for VLMs; (ii) benchmarked 9 frontier closed-source models and 13 open-weight models; and (iii) provided a detailed analysis of their failure modes. Code, the stored model outputs, and a pipeline that regenerates the benchmark from the source datasets are available at https://github.com/royerlab/celltrack-bench.
title: CellTrack-Bench: Microscopic Cell Tracking Benchmark for Vision-Language Models

summary: Multilingual language models can give different identity judgments when the same people's names are written in different scripts. We study this effect using 601 audited identity pairs with attested Devanagari and Latin forms, holding the question and relation fixed. Qwen2.5-7B's same-person accuracy falls from 35.1% in Latin to 8.5% in Devanagari under Marathi prompts, while different-person accuracy remains above 98%. Evaluation across five models reveals distinct response biases, and reduced tokenization fragmentation does not reliably close the gap. Replicating the design on 374 audited Malayalam pairs built from the same entities reproduces the effect in a second script and language family: same-person accuracy falls to 5.3%, about half the matched Devanagari rate, while the margin still ranks matching above non-matching names at 0.925 AUROC. Latin-trained probes recover label information from Devanagari states, exceeding a string-feature baseline under similarity-matched negatives. Scalar calibration recovers 87% of the raw model-probe balanced-accuracy gap, identifying decision criterion placement as a major contributor. Activation patching localises causal sensitivity to the second entity in Qwen's middle layers; one shared sensitivity direction transfers about half the full-state margin correction. A fact-independent intervention at this site raises held-out Marathi same-person accuracy from 6.5% to 33.5%, with 98.5% different-person accuracy. Together, these results distinguish script-dependent discrimination from criterion placement and identify a causal site for improving identity judgments.
title: Same Entity, Different Script: Diagnosing Cross-Script Entity Matching Failures in Language Models

summary: Computer-use agents increasingly handle private information and act on users' behalf across desktop and web applications, including email. Phishing therefore poses privacy and security risks that depend not only on whether agents recognize malicious messages, but also on how they respond. Existing phishing datasets were developed primarily for conventional detection, leaving agent susceptibility to persuasive malicious requests insufficiently characterized. To expose vulnerabilities that pre-existing datasets may miss, we introduce AgentPhishing, a benchmark for evaluating whether persuasive phishing attacks can evade detection and induce LLM email agents to comply with malicious requests. We develop PhishOpt, which optimizes reusable email-generation skills against individual agents under fixed benchmark constraints and a realism constraint. We analyze the generated emails using Cialdini's persuasion principles to identify strategies associated with agent failures and use these findings to construct a universal generation skill. Our evaluation shows that agents can handle pre-existing phishing emails safely yet remain susceptible to attacks adapted to agent behavior, while in an AgentPhishing evaluation of nine agents, four exhibit phishing-detection rates below $10\%$ and malicious-request compliance rates above $45\%$. These results highlight the limits of inferring agent safety from conventional phishing evaluations and the need to assess how agents respond to persuasive malicious requests.
title: AgentPhishing: A Benchmark of LLM Email Agents Under Adaptive Attack

summary: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites are vital in providing seamless connectivities to ground users (GUs). However, complex satellite-to-ground propagation and non-negligible satellite failure probabilities make single-satellite transmission unreliable. To address this issue, we consider a multi-LEO-satellite communication network (mLEO-CN), where a typical GU is served by multiple LEO satellites. The satellite locations are modeled as a binomial point process on a sphere and ordered according to their distances to the GU. To improve communication reliability, a serial communication scheme is adopted, in which the subsequent satellite is activated only when all preceding satellites fail to satisfy the target signal-to-noise ratio threshold. By employing the tool of stochastic geometry, we derive key performance metrics, including overall transmission success probability, average transmission rate, and end-to-end delay under the serial communication scheme by incorporating both shadowed Rician (SR) fading and satellite failure probabilities. To improve analytical tractability, we derive asymptotic expressions for the end-to-end transmission success probability in two special cases by leveraging the asymptotic expression of the SR fading model and a Gamma-distribution, and further propose a cluster-based approximation approach for the overall transmission success probability. Building on these analyses, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the ratio of the overall transmission success probability to the end-to-end delay, and obtain its solution using a one-dimensional search approach. Numerical results validate the analysis, reveal the impact of key parameters, and identify the optimal number of serving LEO satellites under different constellation altitudes.
title: Stochastic Geometry Analysis and Optimization for Multi-LEO Satellite-Assisted Communications

summary: Many deployments require a model to move rapidly from a data-rich source to a related target observed only sparsely. This is especially consequential where target data are difficult to collect, as in healthcare settings with persistent population or acquisition imbalances. Retraining or fine-tuning a high-capacity generator for every target is costly and can be statistically unreliable when target data are scarce. We introduce Meta-Diff, which instead learns a recurring source--target relation once in a compact task space. A shared encoder maps each distribution to a low-dimensional coordinate; a learned relation transports a new source coordinate to its predicted target, and a shared diffusion backbone generates from that prediction without target-specific retraining. Controlled Gaussian-mixture experiments identify when this works: task identity must survive the representation, the relation must generalise across tasks, and the source--target shift must leave useful headroom for transport. On held-out CIFAR-100 validation tasks, correct source $+$ transport achieves 13.9% lower mean SW than transport from the wrong source. With validation-selected adaptation settings in the final-test one-target comparison, its mean SW is 14.7% lower than target-only modelling and 32.7% lower than full fine-tuning; the main route itself uses no target image and assumes the applicable relation is known. On matched CIFAR test episodes, generating from the clean-source coordinate and then applying the known corruption yields lower SW than task-space transport. Office-Home exposes a complementary boundary: transport can align target-domain statistics without reliable object identity. Together, these results recast extreme-few-shot adaptation as reusable transport in task space, while making the conditions for its success and failure directly measurable.
title: Bridging the Data Gap: Source-Informed Task-Space Transport for Few-Shot Diffusion

summary: Differential Privacy (DP) has become a prominent approach for protecting graph data releases, yet empirical auditing methodologies have largely been developed for tabular datasets and machine learning pipelines rather than graph-structured outputs. We present a methodology for empirically auditing DP graph release mechanisms, identifying two graph-specific audit design problems: canary construction and witness statistic selection. We combine these components with an established statistically certified testing procedure and implement the resulting methodology as an open-source Python toolkit. To demonstrate the approach, we audit a published state-of-the-art Node-DP graph release mechanism. Across a series of synthetic and real-world canary pairs, we obtain certified lower bounds on the privacy parameter {\varepsilon} that exceed the claimed value, yielding counterexamples sufficient to falsify the claimed guarantee for the audited implementation. The violations persist under progressively stronger restrictions on the input domain, including non-empty and connected graphs. We also show that witness selection can materially affect whether a violation is detected, highlighting the importance of evaluating a diverse battery of statistics when auditing DP graph release mechanisms.
title: Practical Auditing of Differentially Private Graph Release Mechanisms: Methodology, Toolkit, and Case Study

summary: Detailed image captioning is usually framed as an amount problem: a model should mention more visual facts while avoiding hallucination. However, autoregressive VLMs generate captions as ordered sequences, and later generations may be produced under weaker or noisier visual grounding. We therefore argue that long-form captioning should be studied not only by what facts are mentioned, but also by where they appear. We introduce a position-aware rubric representation that decomposes dense human references into atomic visual claims, verifies generated captions against those claims, and induces a quartile-wise composition of supported, hallucinated, and generic content. This lens reveals two qualitatively different failures in long captions: models tend to produce unsupported specificity in the middle, while the final portion often escapes into vague, non-evidential language rather than simply accumulating more hallucination. A same-reference human control does not exhibit these patterns; additional human audits examine the visual validity of the induced labels. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose PAGER (Position-Aware Grounded Evidence Reinforcement), a GRPO training objective with separate signals for supported fine-grained middle evidence, evidence-bearing tail continuation, claim coverage, and content-aware length control. The result is a closed loop: the same ordered claim representation identifies where long captions fail and supplies the position-specific reward needed to repair those failures. Experiments on detailed-caption benchmarks show that PAGER improves position-wise grounding and pairwise caption preference while preserving competitive global caption quality.
title: Where Do Long Captions Fail? Position-Aware Diagnosis and Reinforcement Learning for Detailed Image Captioning

summary: In standard acoustic anomaly detection (ASD), models are usually trained separately for each machine or domain using explicit metadata. However, in realistic deployments, machine identifiers are incomplete, unreliable, or simply unavailable. Thus, metadata-free machinery ASD asks a single model to monitor mixed machine populations without machine IDs. In this paper, we argue that the main failure mode is not a weak detector family, but representation entanglement. The heterogeneous normal modes overlap in frozen pre-trained feature spaces, making anomaly scoring and approximate retrieval unreliable. We study this problem directly and propose HARMONY (Hierarchical Anchor Retrieval on Manifold for Oblivious-source acoustic aNomalY detection), an anchor-guided geometric repartitioning framework that reorganizes mixed-source features into compact Voronoi regions and reuses this structure for hierarchical retrieval. On DCASE 2020, HARMONY improves mean AUC from 75.40% to 90.00% (14.60 percentage points) over the strongest unified baseline and from 83.90% to 90.00% over a strong foundation-feature baseline. On a single CPU, its hierarchical retrieval achieves a 7.8x speedup over exhaustive search with only a 0.20 percentage-point AUC drop. These results suggest that incorporating explicit geometric partitioning can improve both detection accuracy and retrieval efficiency for ASD. Code is available at https://github.com/Zzyh0208/HARMONY.
title: HARMONY: Hierarchical Anchor Retrieval on Manifold for Oblivious-source Machinery Acoustic Anomaly Detection

summary: The work builds a foundation of physics from a single assumption: everything is a process, and a process is an ideal sine; its centre, the balance, is the observer. Only the square — intensity without phase — passes between levels; from this arise dimensions, the arrow of time, the quantum and the standard. On this basis stable particles are built as standing waves together with their galactic analogues, the initial rules of quantum mechanics and relativity are derived, and the constants are linked to a single number — the speed of light. Agreement with experiment is at the level of a few percent; the model attributes the discrepancies to the imperfection of the standard. Main results The four stable particles (neutrino, electron, neutron, proton) are the four stable states of a standing wave; masses from the speed of light alone: electron +0.7 %, nucleons about −3 % [result given hypotheses]. The Born rule, the randomness of a single outcome, the 2√2 limit in the Bell test, spin ½ and g = 2 [result]. The Lorentz transformation from the “speed budget” c² = v² + v_int², the Klein — Gordon and Schrödinger equations, Schwarzschild gravitational time dilation and the light deflection of 1.75″ [result]. Similarity of the small and the large with the step c⁴: the image of the neutron is the stellar mass of the Milky Way (5.5·10¹⁰ versus (6.1 ± 1.1)·10¹⁰ solar masses) [hypothesis, numerical agreement]. The large end is built by the same logic as the microworld: the construction yields the Hubble constant H₀ = 1/(5c²) ≈ 68.7 km/s/Mpc and the smallest acceleration of galaxies a₀ = 1/(10πc) [result given hypotheses]. The gravitational constant G ≈ c^(−6/5) (0.8 %); the mass of the Universe and the scale of dark energy are expressed through c [hypothesis]. The fine-structure constant has been found as the number 1/α ≈ 4·(c/2π)^(1/5) (0.22 %); its meaning is open [observation]. Limitations: the accuracy is percent-level, not parts per million; the standard and several constants remain open questions. The status of each statement is given in the text. Revision dated 2026-10-23:   Version 23.4 — revision of Part IV (§11–§12): the construction of stable particles is now derived from rules obtained earlier, and no hypotheses remain in these sections. Resonance is refined (the number of points of correspondence is set by the level of the box: 2, 4, 8), as are the anchors of the standards (half a cycle for time, a quarter for length).       Работа строит основу физики из одного допущения: всё — процесс, а процесс — идеальный синус; его центр, баланс, — наблюдатель. Между уровнями проходит только квадрат — интенсивность без фазы; отсюда рождаются измерения, стрела времени, квант и эталон. На этой основе построены стабильные частицы как стоячие волны и их галактические аналоги, выведены исходные правила квантовой механики и относительности, а постоянные связаны с одним числом — скоростью света. Совпадения с опытом — на уровне процентов; расхождения модель относит к неидеальности эталона. Основные результаты Четыре стабильные частицы (нейтрино, электрон, нейтрон, протон) — четыре устойчивых состояния стоячей волны; массы из одной скорости света: электрон +0,7 %, нуклоны около −3 % [результат при гипотезах]. Правило Борна, случайность отдельного исхода, предел 2√2 в проверке Белла, спин ½ и g = 2 [результат]. Преобразование Лоренца из «бюджета скорости» c² = v² + v_вн², уравнения Клейна — Гордона и Шрёдингера, гравитационное замедление времени по Шварцшильду и отклонение света 1,75″ [результат]. title: The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton

summary: We study intermediate sample-size efficiency for censored regression tests when the signal and significance level both tend to zero. Independent treatment assignment permits finite-sample conditional sign calibration under arbitrary outcome dependence. For stationary ergodic latent fields with independent smooth site noise, bounded scores learned from the same pooled outcomes retain their first-order drift under empirical squared-error consistency, without an estimation-rate requirement. An observable censored rank procedure consequently admits an explicit leading cost on long-range dependent fields with nonsummable covariances. Smooth response scores admit a complementary result without independent site noise. For observational fields, separated blocks and paired variance calibration control the dependence approximation at the nominal testing level and yield sample-size costs under explicit absolute-regularity envelopes. An exactly centered censored contrast removes unknown marginal centering under stated exogeneity conditions. We also give a product-limit construction for independent random censoring, information-loss identities, and directional score-bank comparisons. Numerical studies distinguish procedure loss, score-learning loss, and spatial variance inflation. A stationary nonergodic counterexample and an uncensored Gaussian benchmark delimit the field results. Independent-data proofs, finite-range constructions, and a finite-dimensional measurement extension are included in the same manuscript.
tags: censored regression; intermediate efficiency; long-range dependence; random field; randomization test; rank statistic.
title: Intermediate efficiency of censored regression tests on stationary random fields

summary: Video diffusion models have learned rich 3D/4D priors, making them promising for scene generation and video re-rendering. However, their use in spatial tasks is limited by imprecise camera control, spatial and temporal inconsistencies, and entangled camera motion with scene dynamics. Existing approaches, such as task-specific fine-tuning and post-process warping, often introduce visual artifacts, generalize poorly, or incur high computational costs. We propose WorldForge V2 to achieve accurate camera control while preserving the generative capabilities of pretrained video models. We first develop a training-free guidance framework using warped references to iteratively refine generation along a target camera path. Optical-flow analysis identifies motion-related latent channels for selective guidance, helping separate motion control from appearance. A dual-path strategy further compares guided and unguided predictions to correct artifacts from imperfect references. Together, these components guide viewpoint changes while preserving scene appearance and object motion. To reduce refinement costs, v-cache approximates the correction using the preceding denoising prediction, avoiding an additional model evaluation. We further extend motion localization from latent channels to network blocks and introduce Trajectory LoRA, which concentrates adaptation on blocks most responsive to trajectory guidance. A two-stage training strategy teaches these adapters to denoise the states encountered during guided generation, using limited supervision effectively. This enables reliable camera control with very little training data, with a single training scene already supporting generalization to unseen scenes. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations across multiple datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art generation quality and trajectory accuracy in camera-controlled video generation.
title: WorldForge V2: Eliciting Camera-Trajectory Alignment in Video Diffusion Models

summary: Ray tracing (RT) generates photorealistic images by simulating the physical behavior of light as it interacts with surfaces in a virtual scene. In film production and high-end rendering pipelines, this technique computes global illumination, reflections, refractions, and soft shadows by tracing millions of light rays per frame and accurately modeling their bounces and attenuation. Contemporary GPUs incorporate specialized ray tracing hardware to accelerate key operations in the traversal pipeline. By accelerating these stages in hardware, the unit enables real-time ray tracing for complex scenes that previously required offline computation. However, ray tracing introduces substantial control and data divergence. Each ray may traverse a different set of nodes in the acceleration structure, encounter distinct materials, or terminate at varying depths. This irregularity reduces thread coherence and exposes a fundamental disparity between the GPU SIMT and per-thread execution model of dedicated RT units, where each ray progresses independently. In this work, we seek to validate assumptions made in open-source infrastructure and identify potential inefficiencies in resource management within the ray tracing pipeline. To address inefficiency caused by mismatches between SIMT and RT granularities, we propose Ray-by-Ray, which decomposes on-chip buffers into the granularity of individual rays and introduces lightweight management structures that enable more warps to run in parallel without increasing buffer capacity. This approach improves ray tracing unit utilization and increases memory-level parallelism. Experimental results show that Ray-by-Ray achieves an average performance improvement of 1.91x over the baseline, with an area overhead of 0.19\%.
title: Ray-by-Ray: Fine-Grained Resource Management for GPU Ray Tracing Units

summary: Radio access network (RAN) telemetry reveals radio conditions, protocol behavior, and their consequences for applications. Evaluating its usefulness requires controlled impairments and observations of the same execution. We present C and Python channel brokers and a fault injection workflow for software 5G testbeds connecting an OCUDU base station and a software UE through ZeroMQ. The brokers apply scheduled, directional transformations to I/Q samples and restore the link, while the workflow jointly records applied faults, native and programmable (codelet) telemetry, and application delay. We demonstrate this capability through 45 comparative trials of brief uplink interruptions and stepped additive noise. These use cases distinguish recognizing a radio change from measuring its service consequence: native missing-feedback events retrospectively identify interruptions, whereas noise changes decoding-error measurements without producing those events. Median on-time round-trip times remain near 30 ms, but the prespecified comparisons show mean increases in on-time 95th-percentile delay of 354 and 604 ms for one and five interruptions, and 113 ms for noise. Adding receive-side radio link control (RLC) codelet summaries did not improve interruption classification on held-out trials. The framework provides a reusable way to evaluate measurement choices under known radio faults, before using them in monitoring or learning systems.
title: Controlled Radio Fault Injection and Telemetry Evaluation for Open 5G RANs

summary: We develop an end-to-end framework for assessing a quantum-computing application in industrial materials science: the screening of strongly correlated oxygen-electrode materials for SOFCs and SOECs. We formulate the materials problem in terms of interface observables including oxygen-vacancy formation energies, vacancy migration barriers, and electronic conductivity. We describe how these observables can be obtained using a diagrammatic GW-based embedding, either GW+DMFT or self-energy embedding theory (SEET), applied to a DFT-screened shortlist. The atomistic electrode/electrolyte interface defines the electronic structure problem from which the correlated impurity models are constructed. Quantum impurity solvers would provide the finite-temperature impurity Green's functions required by the embedding. The computational challenges that classical solvers may encounter as the interacting active space grows, together with the polynomial scaling of quantum Hamiltonian simulation for efficiently represented discretized models, open an opportunity for quantum advantage. We identify the benchmarks needed to assess this opportunity through convergence of vacancy and migration energetics and comparison with the best applicable classical solvers. We provide illustrative logical qubit counts and identify the thermal state preparation, simulation, measurement, and repeated-solve costs needed for a complete resource assessment. We connect microscopic observables to macroscopic engineering metrics using a continuum model for mixed ionic--electronic conducting oxygen electrodes that couples oxygen surface exchange, solid-state oxygen transport, electrode microstructure, and finite electrode thickness. Finally, we estimate the potential worldwide business value of improved electrode materials under SOFC and SOEC deployment scenarios informed by public technical targets and electrolyser deployment data.
title: Screening strongly correlated materials in solid oxide cells with quantum simulation

summary: Commit messages help developers understand code changes and support software maintenance. Recent approaches use repository context to improve commit message generation (CMG) with large language models (LLMs). However, existing CMG methods provide limited support for understanding how local edits affect functionality jointly implemented by multiple code entities. This functional understanding is essential for generating commit messages that explain the main change and its impact. To address this problem, we propose CAMGen, a core change-aware multi-view commit message generation framework that incorporates functional context into generation. CAMGen identifies core entities that represent the primary change intent. It then forms candidate functional units through repository-wide semantic clustering and uses those containing the core entities to construct a Functional Semantic View. This view supplies semantic context for interpreting the affected functionality. CAMGen also uses context provided by the Structural Dependency View and the Historical Exemplar View. The context from all three views is then provided to the LLM together with the code diff to guide CMG. The experimental results show that CAMGen outperforms representative CMG baselines across three programming languages. Human evaluation further shows that CAMGen generates more complete commit messages with clearer explanations of change rationale and impact. These results demonstrate the value of functional context and complementary repository information for CMG.
title: CAMGen: A Core Change-Aware Multi-View Framework for Commit Message Generation

summary: Local anomaly detection is the task of identifying spatially confined anomalous or out-of-distribution (OOD) regions within an otherwise in-distribution (ID) image. Most existing methods are designed for a specific context, with a strong focus on industrial defect detection, where they achieve excellent performance on well-established benchmarks. However, we observe that these methods can exhibit significant performance drops in other contexts, especially when the inlier distribution is multimodal. To account for this inlier complexity, we propose LACToS, a principled local OOD detection method based on statistical typicality and made tractable through two innovations: (i) grouping pixels into superpixels and (ii) using a computationally efficient proxy to estimate typicality. We evaluate LACToS across three diverse applications spanning medical imaging, human faces, and X-ray security screening. LACToS performs more robustly than prior methods across these benchmarks. The code is released here: https://github.com/voilalab/LACToS.
title: LACToS: Local Anomaly Detection via Conditional Typicality of Superpixels

summary: Metaphor is a crucial aspect of human cognition. As such, we would like to understand how it is represented in large language models (LLMs) and how it might be controlled. We use mechanistic interpretability techniques to identify causal subspaces in a range of LLMs covering different architectures and sizes. We show that we are able to steer output on classification tasks across different parts of speech. We are also able to steer output on generation tasks, indicating that these techniques can be used to control the metaphoricity of LLM output.
title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models

summary: Processed single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data for “Selective Immune Silencing by Targeted TGF-β Mimics” This record contains processed sequencing data, derived analysis objects, and analysis code supporting the transcriptomic analyses in Sun, Ogishi, Barrett, Jiang, Yan et al., Selective Immune Silencing by Targeted TGF-β Mimics . The study repurposes the helminth-derived TGF-β mimic TGM1 as a cell-type-targeted immunosuppressant by replacing its CD44-binding domains 4–5 with high-affinity targeting modules. Constructs targeting mouse or human CD4 or CD8α, or human CD19, are designed to preferentially deliver TGF-β receptor agonism to selected lymphocyte subsets. Two datasets are included, each as a separate archive. 1. Single-cell RNA-seq of B-cell-enriched samples from human spleen organoids (raw reads: GEO GSE346912). Human spleen organoids from two deceased organ donors (Sp88, 33-year-old female; Sp99, 53-year-old male) were stimulated with live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) in the presence of vehicle, untargeted low-affinity TGM1 (domains 1–3), or the CD19-targeted TGF-β agonist TGM1-hCD19, alongside unstimulated controls (4 conditions × 2 donors = 8 samples). On day 7, B cells were enriched by negative selection, captured on a 10x Genomics Chromium X instrument using Single Cell 5′ R2-only v3 chemistry, and sequenced as paired-end 150-bp reads on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Reads were aligned to GRCh38-2024-A and quantified with Cell Ranger v9.0.1, with intronic reads included, recovering approximately 14,000–27,000 cells per sample. After quality control in Seurat v5.3.1, 163,632 cells were retained (33,179 mock; 51,696 LAIV; 43,858 LAIV + untargeted TGM1; 34,899 LAIV + TGM1-hCD19), of which 130,987 were B-lineage cells. Cell-type annotation combined Louvain clustering, label transfer from the Human Tonsil Atlas v2 ( https://zenodo.org/records/8373756 ), and manual curation using canonical markers. The record provides Cell Ranger filtered feature-barcode matrices and per-sample QC summaries; cell-type label-transfer and curated annotation tables; differential expression and fgsea results; pySCENIC v0.12.1 regulon activity matrices (265 regulons, including IRF4 and PRDM1/BLIMP1); velocyto loom files and scVelo per-cell velocity outputs underlying the RNA velocity analysis; gene signature and cell-cycle scores; and all R and Python analysis code. These analyses support suppression of the germinal center B-cell–to–plasmablast transition by B-cell-targeted TGF-β agonism, with markedly reduced plasmablast and plasma-cell representation, increased naïve B-cell representation, and IRF4 and PRDM1/BLIMP1 regulon activities approaching unstimulated levels. RNA velocity analyses are consistent with reduced progression through the plasmablast differentiation trajectory. 2. Bulk RNA-seq of antigen-specific mouse CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells (raw reads: GEO GSE346305). Naïve Thy1.1⁺ OT-II (CD4⁺) and OT-I (CD8⁺) T cells were co-transferred into Thy1.1⁻ recipient mice, which were then immunized with ovalbumin emulsified in complete Freund’s adjuvant and treated every other day with PBS, untargeted TGM1, TGM1-mCD4, or TGM1-mCD8 (approximately 40–50 pmol per dose for TGM1 constructs). Donor OT-II and OT-I cells were sorted from draining lymph nodes for RNA sequencing. Naïve OT-II and OT-I cells were included as baseline controls, yielding 20 libraries in total (2 cell types × 5 conditions, comprising 4 treatment groups and 1 naïve control group, × 2 biological replicates). Reads were aligned to mm10 with Rsubread v2.18.0, quantified with featureCounts, and analyzed with DESeq2. Downstream analyses include principal component analysis (PCA) of variance-stabilized counts, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) against Hallmark gene sets, and exploratory immune-cell deconvolution using EPIC with the Monaco ref
title: Selective Immune Silencing by Targeted TGF-β Mimics

summary: Background : The rapid digitisation of allied health education has led to an alarming rise in Digital Eye Strain (DES), also termed Computer Vision Syndrome (CVS), among undergraduate Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) students. Standard therapies like artificial tears provide temporary lubrication without resolving the underlying neuro-vascular tension and oxidative ocular stress. Objectives : To evaluate and compare the therapeutic efficacy of daily Isotonic Saline Jal Neti versus Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash over 4 weeks on digital asthenopia, tear film stability, tear volume, and visual comfort in a cohort of 16 BPT students. Methodology : A 4-week prospective, parallel-group, randomized controlled empirical pilot trial was conducted at Maya Devi University, Dehradun. Sixteen BPT students (aged 18–25) meeting inclusion criteria (screen time ≥ 6 hrs/day, CVS-Q ≥ 6, TBUT < 10 s) were randomized 1:1 into Group A (Jal Neti, n=8) and Group B (Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash, n=8). Outcome metrics assessed at baseline (Day 0) and post-intervention (Day 28) included: Computer Vision Syndrome Questionnaire (CVS-Q), Visual Fatigue Scale (VFS, 0-60), Tear Break-Up Time (TBUT, seconds), and Schirmer’s Test-I (mm/5 min). Results : Both groups exhibited statistically significant intra-group improvements across all parameters (p < 0.001). Group B (Triphala) achieved superior improvement in tear film stability and lacrimal secretion: TBUT increased by +4.15 ± 0.80 s in Group B vs. +2.30 ± 0.60 s in Group A (p < 0.001); Schirmer-I values increased by +4.85 ± 1.10 mm in Group B vs. +2.65 ± 0.85 mm in Group A (p < 0.001). Conversely, Group A (Jal Neti) achieved greater relief from central visual fatigue and periocular headaches: VFS scores decreased by -18.60 ± 2.95 points in Group A vs. -14.25 ± 2.75 points in Group B (p < 0.01). Total CVS-Q scores dropped markedly in both groups (Group A: 12.75 to 5.25; Group B: 13.00 to 4.90). Conclusion : Both modalities significantly alleviate digital eye strain in BPT students. Sterile Triphala eye wash is particularly potent for restoring ocular surface hydration and tear film stability, whereas Jal Neti excels in alleviating deep neuromuscular fatigue and periorbital strain.
tags: Digital Eye Strain, Jal Neti, Triphala, Tear Break-Up Time, Schirmer's Test, Physiotherapy Students, Pilot Study.
title: Comparative Evaluation of Isotonic Saline Jal Neti versus Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash on Digital Asthenopia, Tear Film Dynamics, and Visual Comfort in Undergraduate Physiotherapy Students: A Single-Center Empirical Pilot Study

summary: Data and code deposit Supporting materials for: Kurniawan C, Virgana R, Pratiwi YS, Kartasasmita AS. Mapping resveratrol research across diabetic microvascular complications: a bibliometric analysis of research intensity and themes. Cureus (under review). What this deposit contains The analysis set is 182 unique Scopus records (English articles and reviews, 2016–2025) on resveratrol in diabetic retinopathy (DR), diabetic nephropathy (DN) and diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN). Research intensity is the number of resveratrol records for a complication divided by the number of all Scopus records on the same complication retrieved by the same disease terms without resveratrol terms.
