summary: This study established a decadal baseline (2015) for heavy metal pollution in the Western Lagos Lagoon  (Makoko and UNILAG Waterfront) using the rainbow land crab, Cardisoma armatum, as a sentinel bio monitor. Morphometric analysis revealed significantly large carapace dimensions, suggesting an advanced  age-class or high nutrient loading (eutrophication) rather than environmental stability. While raw tissue  concentrations for Lead (Pb) showed no significant spatial variance (p > 0.05), the Biota-Sediment  Accumulation Factor for Pb was above the 1.0 threshold at both stations, identifying it as the primary  toxicological threat. Conversely, Zinc (Zn) levels remained within safe BSAF limits, consistent with its role  as a regulated essential micronutrient. Biochemical markers (CAT, GST, and MDA) indicated significant  oxidative stress, particularly at the UNILAG site, suggesting a high pollution-induced metabolic burden.  Histopathological examination corroborated these findings, showing a marked reduction in reserved inclusion  cells (R-cells) across both populations, which is a clear signal of metabolic exhaustion as energy is diverted  from somatic growth to detoxification. Physical evidence of organopathy was further observed via hemocyte  plugs in the gills and tubular degradation in the hepatopancreas. These 2015 findings provide a critical  reference point for future longitudinal studies and highlight the urgent need for integrated human health risk  assessments, analysis of reproductive damage due to oxidative stress in the Lagos Lagoon ecosystem.  Keywords- Bio-indicators, BSAF, Cardisoma armatum, Oxidative Stress Biomarkers, Metabolic Exhaustion.
tags: Bio-indicators, BSAF, Cardisoma armatum, Oxidative Stress Biomarkers, Metabolic Exhaustion.
title: A Decadal Baseline of Heavy Metal Bioaccumulation and Oxidative Stress in Cardisoma armatum: A Sentinel Assessment of the Western Lagos Lagoon

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-five entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.
title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

summary: **GLOBES — Global Library of Observations from Buoys for Evaluating Sea States** GLOBES is a global dataset of historical wave observations from moored buoys, developed to improve the accessibility, consistency, and reuse of in situ wave measurements across observing networks. The dataset integrates **1,665 buoy records from 27 data providers across 41 countries**, representing 19,469 station-years of observations spanning 1969–2026. Records retain their native temporal resolution, ranging from 10 minutes to 3 hours, and include up to seven standardized wave parameters: significant wave height (HS), maximum wave height (HM), peak wave period (TP), zero-crossing wave period (TZ), mean wave period (TM), wave direction (DR), and directional spread (SP). GLOBES harmonizes timestamps, units, missing-value conventions, station metadata, and quality-control flags while preserving original provider information and data provenance. The archive is distributed as standardized station-based files, accompanied by provider-specific quality-control information where available. **Data organization:** This release contains 28 compressed archives representing 27 data providers. NOWPHAS observations are distributed separately at 20-minute and 2-hour temporal resolutions, resulting in 1,745 distributed time series. **Release status:** This is a preliminary data release (v0.1.0). Metadata, documentation, and data files may be refined in subsequent versions. **Data use and licensing:** GLOBES integrates observations subject to different provider-specific licensing, attribution, and usage conditions. Users must consult the USAGE metadata field of individual records and comply with the applicable original provider requirements. No single open license applies to the entire dataset. GLOBES supports research on wave climate, variability and extremes, coastal hazards, and the evaluation of numerical models, hindcasts, reanalyses, and satellite-derived wave products.
title: GLOBES: the Global Library of Observations from Buoys for Evaluating Sea States

summary: IrrMapper is a Random Forest classification of Landsat imagery that maps irrigated agriculture each year at 30 m across Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, New Mexico, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming. This deposit is the GeoTIFF release of version 1.2, the product served in the Google Earth Engine public data catalog as UMT/Climate/IrrMapper_RF/v1_2. One zip per state holds one cloud-optimized GeoTIFF per year (450 files; California begins in 1986), the state boundary polygon used for clipping, and grids.json describing every state's raster grid. Values: 1 irrigated, 0 not irrigated, 255 nodata. All files are in EPSG:5070 (NAD83 / Conus Albers) at 30 m on one shared pixel lattice, so all years of a state stack without resampling and neighboring states align pixel for pixel. SHA256 checksums are provided for every GeoTIFF and archive. See README.md for the format, grid definition, provenance and known limitations.
title: IrrMapper v1.2: annual 30 m irrigated-agriculture maps of 11 western US states, 1985-2025

summary: This protocol presents a systematic, deterministic translation framework for Beinecke MS 408 (The Voynich Manuscript). The framework interprets the manuscript as a 15th-century reverse-indexed chemical and pharmaceutical register produced within an Alpine/Central European workshop tradition. By operating on a phonetic-Latin reconstruction model, the cipher maps Extensible Alphabet Code (EVA) glyphs to a rigid, cross-sectional technical vocabulary. The validity of this protocol is verified through a 4-stage empirical pipeline featuring dual botanical cross-validation (Dragon's Blood resin vs. Opium Poppy latex) and external vernacular anchor verification via the marginalia on Folio 116v.
title: Voynich Manuscript Final Decoding Procedure

summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

summary: We study intransitive probabilistic preferences through dice whose face labels may be repeated. We distinguish restricted models, in which the set of permitted labels depends on the number of sides, from the unrestricted model, which allows arbitrary integer labels. We review existence results, including the exceptional impossibility of a Chinese chain of five four-sided dice, and give an explicit construction establishing the known existence of simple cycles of three-sided dice of every length m ≥3, with no ties and a net win margin of one. We examine mixed-integer programming, simulated annealing, and lexicographic optimization of the margins. We then extend pairwise comparison to probability measures by means of bounded, measurable, antisymmetric kernels. For complete comparison data with uniform weights, we derive the Hodge decomposition of the margin matrix into an additive score component and an orthogonal, divergence-free residual. We distinguish the failure of an exact additive representation from the existence of strict preference cycles. The minimax theorem ensures that every finite family admits a mixed strategy with nonnegative expected margin against every mixture of that family. For the historical cycle with margins 4, 4, 10, we compute both the decomposition and the equilibrium mixture (2/9, 5/9, 2/9). Applications to portfolios, artistic evaluation, visual perception, and sports clarify the distinctions among independent comparisons, shared scenarios, and expected utility.
title: Chinese and Mayan Dice: Circular Chains, Explicit Constructions, and Decision Theory

summary: Mitoscope MitoScope is a scalable end-to-end workflow for long-read specific mtDNA and NUMT analysis. MitoScope integrates five key modules: 1) mtDNA selection, 2) variant calling and annotation, 3) assembly generation, 4) quality control, and 5) optional NUMT profiling. It is written using Nextflow and fully containerized using Singularity images. It can be run on either ONT or PacBio data and accepts raw sequencing data or aligned reads as input. mitoScope is currently in active development. Open an issue if you find a problem or have a suggestion. Table of Contents Installation Usage Outputs Installation Pre-requisites Nextflow Singularity Setup VERSION=0.5.0 wget https://github.com/czakarian/mitoscope/archive/refs/tags/v${VERSION}.tar.gz tar xvf v${VERSION}.tar.gz && rm v${VERSION}.tar.gz cd mitoscope-${VERSION}/ Usage nextflow run /path/to/mitoscope-${VERSION}/main.nf -params-file example_params.yaml Parameters Specifications The required -params-file argument accepts a yaml file with the following parameter specifications. See below or example_params.yaml for example. | name | description | |-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | samplesheet | Path to a headerless csv file with 1) sample ids & 2) input file paths | | input_type | Input type (options are: 'bam', 'cram', 'fastq', 'fastq.gz'). | | is_aligned | Set to true if input is aligned, otherwise set to false. | | platform | Specify 'pb' for PacBio or 'ont' for ONT. | | outdir | Path to directory to output results. | | reference | Path to reference genome. | example_params.yaml samplesheet: "samples.csv" input_type: "bam" is_aligned: true platform: "pb" outdir: "/path/to/output/dir/result" reference: "/path/to/ref/for/cram/GRCH38.fa" Optional Parameters To call non-reference NUMT candidates, add numt_profiling: true to the yaml file. This functionality is turned off by default to otherwise reduce computational load and is only available for use with aligned input. To skip methylation related NUMT filtration and methylation calling add skip_methylation: true to the yaml file. This can be used to process long-read amplicon sequencing data or other long-read data that lacks methylation calls. Sample Manifest One of the required parameters in the yaml file is the path to a sample manifest ( samplesheet ). See below or example_sample_manifest.csv for example. samples.csv sample1,/path/to/sample1.bam sample2,/path/to/sample2.bam sample3,/path/to/sample3.bam sample4,/path/to/sample4.bam Outputs Mitoscope outputs a directory for each sample with the following subdirectories. | name | description | |----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------- | | alignments/ | Bam files for retained mtDNA reads and discarded reads. | | assembly/ | Assembly output from meta-flye. | | methylation/ | Methylation calls from modkit/pb-CpG-tools. | | numts/ | Non-reference NUMT candidates. | | qc/ | QC metrics. | | variants/ | Variant calls (snv/indel, SV) | | logs/ | Log files. |
title: github.com/czakarian/mitoscope

summary: Every LLM request SWAN AI-SQL (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWAN-AISQL) and the baselines issue on SemBench MOVIE/ECOMM/MMQA, the 30-query hybrid bench of the PLOP paper and the SWAN 2.0 benchmark (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWANBench), with the provider's answer, its measured latency and its cost, as a DuckDB file (gzip-compressed, 0.96 GB; 4.4 GB unpacked; 2,409,502 recorded calls) for the repository's cache proxy (serve/ai_cache_server.py). It holds SWAN AI-SQL, LOTUS 1.2.4, PLOP (the public Morrila fork, DP cost-model mode), BlendSQL 0.1.27, ThalamusDB 0.1.15 (exact mode) and Palimpzest 1.5.3 (Abacus optimizer) on every benchmark each of them runs. SWAN AI-SQL's recordings are its current ones (2026-10-23, DuckDB 2.0.0); every SWAN 2.0 recording is a fresh run through an empty cache (LOTUS and PLOP on 2026-10-03, BlendSQL and Palimpzest on 2026-10-05, SWAN AI-SQL on 2026-10-23). Always use the latest version: the concept DOI and serve/fetch_cache.sh resolve to it. Every table in the repositories replays without a provider key: run serve/fetch_cache.sh (it downloads, checks and unpacks the latest version), then the benchmark harnesses; the proxy replays each recorded answer with its recorded latency and cost. Model: gpt-5.6-luna, temperature 0, each system's default prompts (zero-shot). Replay matches requests byte for byte; an edited query, another model, or a client library that renders the request differently is a fresh request. The systems' own run-to-run variance (LOTUS's ranking order, result assembly in BlendSQL and Palimpzest, ThalamusDB's sampler, PLOP's parallel operator order) is theirs, not the cache's.
title: SWAN AI-SQL replay cache: recorded gpt-5.6-luna answers of SWAN, LOTUS, BlendSQL, Palimpzest, ThalamusDB and PLOP on SemBench, the PLOP hybrid bench and SWAN 2.0

summary: Malaria early-warning systems that treat climate as a spatially uniform forcing mis-time vector-control deployment when the thermal niche of Anopheles vectors shifts across districts. The framework is formalised as a structural causal model over a district-month lattice, with a graph-identification condition and a lag-recovery theorem that bounds timing error by the spectral gap of the estimated adjacency matrix. A climate-analytics evaluation is conducted on NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E), 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 °C and a standard deviation of 1.043 °C; the estimated linear trend was −0.1564 °C per decade. The evaluation shows that a causal graph that admits lagged hydrological mediators recovers the intervention window with lower timing error than a temperature-only baseline, and that the error bound tightens as the spectral gap widens. The contribution is a formal link between causal-graph identifiability and the operational quantity that public-health managers actually care about: how many weeks early or late a spraying or net-distribution campaign is triggered.
tags: malaria early warning; causal graph learning; spatiotemporal modelling; climate analytics; intervention timing; vector-range shift; Uganda
title: Spatiotemporal causal graph learning for malaria early-warning under climate-driven vector-range shifts: a climate-analytics evaluation of intervention-timing error

summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.
tags: physics-informed neural networks; rainfall extremes; tail-index distortion; dam safety; radiosonde initialization; climate analytics; downscaling
title: Physics-informed neural networks for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes under sparse radiosonde initialization: a climate-analytics evaluation of tail-index distortion in dam-safety analytics

summary: National methane inventories increasingly rely on satellite-constrained plume inversion, yet the placement of a fixed sensor budget across a landscape of sparse satellite revisits determines how much of the resulting emission-attribution error is reducible and how much is structural. the present analysis formalises budget-constrained sensor placement as a submodular maximisation problem over a plume-inversion error functional, derives a greedy placement rule with a (1 - 1/e) approximation guarantee under a monotone submodular surrogate, and characterises the conditions under which the surrogate diverges from the true attribution error. The analysis is methodological and theoretical: no field deployment is reported. A worked evaluation on a computed plume field calibrated to published satellite revisit statistics shows that the greedy rule recovers between 71 and 88 per cent of the oracle placement gain across budget levels, while the residual attribution error is dominated by revisit sparsity rather than by sensor count. Inventory audits should report a placement-attributable error component separately from a revisit-attributable component, because conflating the two leads auditors to over-attribute residual uncertainty to instrumentation and under-attribute it to orbital sampling. The contribution is a formal decomposition of emission-attribution error into placement-reducible and revisit-structural parts, together with a placement algorithm whose guarantees are stated relative to that decomposition.
tags: methane plume inversion; sensor placement; submodular optimisation; satellite revisit; emission attribution; inventory audit; computer science
title: Budget-constrained sensor placement for methane plume inversion under sparse satellite revisits: a computer-science evaluation of emission-attribution error in national inventory audits

summary: HIGH-INTEGRITY CARGO TRANSPORT AND CONTROLLED RELEASE IN MICRO/NANOROBOTICS AT THE LIMIT English Introduction This high-density research monograph develops a falsifiable architecture for high-integrity microrobotic cargo transport and controlled release. Its core coupling is binding kinetics × transport exposure × triggered release. Arrival is explicitly separated from delivery: one identified cargo lineage must remain bound through transport, stay below registered shear thermal and chemical exposure limits, avoid premature leakage and cross-contamination, release inside the authorized spatial and temporal window, preserve a cargo-specific functional endpoint, and leave a closed record of residual material and carrier recovery. The central contribution is the Cargo Integrity Passport, a replayable evidence object that binds cargo and carrier identities, initial load, binding calibration, route, exposure waveforms, leakage samples, trigger fields, target masks, released mass, functional assays, contamination panels, unreleased residue, retrieval, abstentions, failures, and final disposition. Thirty physicalized derivations connect directly to 82 chapters, 410 single-page research studies, 200 Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. When unknown shear pulses, constrictions, sham triggers, second cargo lots, and carrier aging are introduced blindly, the system must lower both premature leakage and nonrelease rather than exchange one failure for the other. Missing mass, destructive triggering, target expansion, and deleted failed cargo reject the claim.

summary: Biomimetic design often risks superficial imitation and functional greenwashing. We introduce the Illusion-Real Biomimicry Index (IRBI), a non-compensatory composite metric bridging the Double Diamond design process. The IRBI synthesizes an evidence-anchored claim ledger (Illusion Index Framework, IIF) with a multi-criteria systemic quality framework (Integrated Biomimicry Impact Evaluation Framework, IBIEF) via a weighted geometric mean equipped with a Heaviside veto trigger. The methodology is evaluated across two tracks. Part A assesses three engineering artefacts (an industrial symbiosis network, a passive sharkskin foil, and an archetypal imitation) under a 10,000-draw Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis over claim measurement uncertainties, AHP weights, and provisional veto thresholds. Part B explores the feasibility of extracting dynamic stability indicators from inertial sensor time series during controlled movements (cervical kinematics, N=1 ). Part A yielded deterministic IRBI scores of 0.90, 0.62, and 0.00 (veto triggered), respectively, demonstrating 100% hierarchical rank preservation. In Part B, amplitude-distribution entropy asymmetry captured postural uncoupling, whereas the Rosenstein Lyapunov slope failed to reject the linearly correlated noise null hypothesis. The IRBI provides a mathematically auditable gatekeeper against greenwashing, while dynamic indicator telemetry requires multi-subject cohort calibration before certification deployment.
title: Biomimicry or Greenwashing? Operationalizing Authenticity via Non-Linear Dynamics

summary: The attribution of downwind rainfall changes to irrigation expansion remains contested because irrigation modifies both surface moisture and boundary-layer thermodynamics, and because satellite retrievals of convective initiation are sparse and noisy. The framework combines a potential-outcomes formulation with a honest random-forest splitting rule that permits effect modification by land-surface and atmospheric covariates. A formal result establishes that the forest estimator is consistent for the conditional average treatment effect when the propensity score is known and the retrieval error is classical, and a sensitivity bound quantifies bias under differential misclassification. The framework is then applied in a methodological evaluation using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023, 312 monthly observations), where the mean temperature was 26.414 °C and the warming trend was 0.1553 °C per decade. The evaluation clarifies the conditions under which downwind rainfall attribution is credible and identifies the retrieval-error regimes in which causal-forest estimates should be preferred to regression-adjustment alternatives.
tags: causal forest; irrigation expansion; convective initiation; satellite retrievals; downwind rainfall; climate analytics; heterogeneous treatment effects
title: Causal forest estimation of irrigation-expansion feedbacks on convective initiation from paired satellite retrievals: a climate-analytics evaluation of downwind rainfall attribution

summary: Drought-index insurance for smallholders relies on weather-station telemetry that is sparse and unevenly distributed, so the index measured at a station can diverge from the losses experienced on a farm. the present analysis treats that divergence as a distribution-free calibration problem and proposes a conformal risk-controlling framework that converts station-level temperature and rainfall records into prediction sets for farm-level drought status with a user-specified bound on the probability of payout error. The framework is developed formally: a nonconformity score is defined on the joint space of station telemetry and farm-level loss indicators, a split-conformal calibration procedure is stated, and a finite-sample guarantee on the marginal payout-error rate is proved under exchangeability. The guarantee is then weakened deliberately to characterise the basis-risk inequity that arises when exchangeability fails across agro-ecological zones, and a zone-conditional calibration scheme is proposed to restore coverage within strata. The argument is illustrated with a reanalysis of NASA POWER monthly air temperature at 2 m for Lagos, Nigeria (6.52° N, 3.38° E), 2000–2023, 312 monthly observations, mean 26.414 °C, standard deviation 0.943 °C, and a warming trend of 0.1553 °C per decade.
tags: drought-index insurance; conformal prediction; basis risk; smallholder agriculture; sparse telemetry; risk control; climate analytics
title: Calibrated risk-controlling prediction sets for smallholder drought-index insurance triggers under sparse weather-station telemetry: a climate-analytics evaluation of basis-risk-induced payout inequity

summary: Carbon-credit methodologies for mangrove restoration typically assume that credited carbon storage persists for a fixed horizon, yet staggered enrollment and unobserved baseline dynamics make permanence risk difficult to identify from satellite time series alone. The framework combines a potential-outcomes model for staggered adoption with a hidden-Markov representation of unobserved baseline loss, and derives bounds on the bias of the conventional permanence deduction. Analysis of the identification conditions shows that the standard deduction is unbiased only when baseline loss is independent of enrollment timing, an assumption that fails whenever enrollment is targeted at high-threat sites. The derived bounds imply that permanence-risk overstatement is increasing in the correlation between enrollment timing and baseline threat, and that the sign of the bias can be recovered from observable enrollment-date and land-cover-covariate patterns. The contribution is a diagnostic that credit issuers can apply to existing registries without new field data, together with a formal statement of the conditions under which the conventional deduction is defensible.
tags: mangrove restoration; carbon credits; additionality; permanence risk; causal inference; Landsat time series; staggered enrollment; artificial intelligence evaluation
title: Causal inference on mangrove-restoration carbon-credit additionality from Landsat time series under staggered enrollment: an artificial intelligence evaluation of permanence-risk overstatement

summary: Conformance vectors for agent execution evidence, and the reference verifier that judges them. This release carries 39 corpus manifests across 38 suites and 2,154 vectors in all, among them the in-toto adversarial-execution-evidence predicate, the in-toto ai-agent-action predicate, an AI generation predicate, the observed-effect predicate, SCITT COSE carriage, signed decision receipts and receipt chains, an anchor-stream verifier, ACS core, artifact binding, MCP response-phase interception, the OWASP MCP verification draft, the W3C per-check reporting format and intake, A2A agent-card canonicalization, delegation lifecycle, authority at dispatch, done contracts and receipts, grader isolation, spoofed tool output, test tampering, and ACI deployments. One binary judges every one of them, selected by the suite each corpus manifest declares. Each corpus digest is listed, recomputed from the vector files, in CORPUS-DIGESTS.txt, which the GitHub release signs and timestamps. The predicate's model is execute-and-attest rather than match-and-assert: a consumer recomputes the outcome from the bytes the statement carries, instead of trusting a verdict the producer asserted about itself. This repository is a second, independently usable implementation of that contract, so that any producer of the predicate type can self-certify and any consumer can reject a lying emitter. For the adversarial-execution-evidence corpus this deposit covers suite revision 32: 288 vectors, of which 63 accept, 223 reject and 2 are indeterminate. Its bytes are fixed by the corpus digest bf3e5befd71640757ff1b3f0af63507364b823b5e3f9059678f72f64a46e11c1 recorded in vectors/MANIFEST.json. A published revision is never mutated in place; a normative change to the predicate, or an addition to the corpus, bumps the revision and regenerates every vector byte-identically from its generators, because the vendored specification's digest is itself a corpus input. The archive is the output of git archive --format=tar.gz --prefix=agent-evidence-vectors-0.25.0/ v0.25.0 and reproduces byte for byte from the signed tag (SHA-256 ffd80cc752769d69ef13745f55cac9ab99d5a3cd5476f19359c2646597290970). The intended use is citation by a conformance requirement. A requirement that names this suite, or any other suite demonstrated to exercise the same conditions, is checkable by a party who trusts neither the producer nor the implementer. Cite this version DOI for a conformance claim; the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22758687 always resolves to the newest release.
title: agent-evidence-vectors: conformance vectors for agent execution evidence

Conventional computational models treat physical configurations as external data structures submitted to an independent processor: conformations are enumerated in an address table, transitions are assigned by ad hoc hopping matrices or stochastic Monte Carlo rules, and empirical parameters are fitted post hoc to bulk observables. While effective for descriptive curve-fitting, that paradigm divorces the representation of a state from the lawful operations that generate and invert it. Whenever a coarse observation projects away an internal degree of freedom, a state-only model mistakes an observational quotient or a scheduling collision for an absolute physical barrier. The research program consolidated in this report—spanning the native binary partner rings, the One Inverter twisted clock, the Way Between three-dimensional conformational compiler, and the tetrahedral diamond-lattice and polyethylene matter readers through §167—establishes a rigorous alternative: compilation is the continuing resolution of local relational constraints, and physical observables are typed readouts of the resulting operator algebra. Rather than postulating an external machine or assigning arbitrary binary labels to particles, the architecture begins with the minimal condition for a distinction to persist without terminal fixed points ( ) and traces the exact algebraic and geometric structures forced at each scale. This progression unfolds across four interconnected operational tiers that preserve an explicit way home at every scale by pairing a quotient difference reader with a retained frame or phase coordinate. In the first tier, the native binary ring and twisted clock establish divided left and right representative hemispheres and forward/reverse faces governed by fixed-point-free involutions. In the second tier, the planar honeycomb route compiler lifts into a three-dimensional control torus where synchronous bond torsions execute a diagonal bypass around blocked planar corners. In the third tier, three-dimensional tetrahedral chains on the diamond lattice form an unbranched two-sheeted mirror quotient across a central reflection plane. In the fourth tier, the local tetrahedral operations and reflection symmetries collapse the 72-state polyethylene rotational-isomeric-state transfer matrix into four scalar coordinates, resolving the inverse parameter problem via a rank-two observable Jacobian. Across all four tiers, the compiler operates through two governing equations that separate the underlying accumulated transformation from the perspective of a particular observer: In the first equation, local reversible increments —whether bit shifts, modular carries, planar turns, or spatial   bond torsions—accumulate relative to a held reference frame . Changing   reorients the global description rigidly without altering any internal relation , while substituting a subword   with an alternative sequence   having the identical running product produces a strictly local transformation whose exterior remains undisturbed. In the second equation, the multiplicity structure   belongs to the object's own relation complex, while a chosen reader   exposes only the projection . An apparent zero in   or a rank deficiency in a planar Jacobian does not imply the absence of a physical continuation; it diagnoses a specific mismatch between the active transformation and the reader's coordinate chart. summary: The Western Balkans as a region of developing economies is volatile in economic development at the same time political instability which brings into attention how economic governance is being impacted by political developments and instabilities. This study aims to examine the relationship between political risk and economic governance in the Western Balkans during the period 2002–2023 by using econometric models and quantitative measurements. The investigations focus on six Western Balkan economies. Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia, utilizing annual country-level panel data from the World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators and World Development Indicators. The paper applies Fixed Effects and Random Effects panel regression models with Government effectiveness used as the dependent variable and representing economic governance, while political stability is used as the main explanatory variable and an inverse proxy for political risk. The control variables include GDP per capita growth, inflation, foreign direct investment, and trade openness. The findings suggest that political stability is positively associated with economic governance, but the relationship is not statistically robust after controlling for country-specific and year-specific effects.
tags: Political risk; economic governance; Western Balkans; government effectiveness; political stability; institutional development
title: Economic Governance Under Political Risk in The Western Balkans: Panel Evidence From 2002–2023

summary: This paper consolidates the Phase and Electromagnetic Coupling programme through twenty-one computational checkpoints, examining connections between phase organisation, electromagnetic response, gravitational sourcing, and optical receiver records within explicitly specified physical models. The analysis connects amplitude and relative phase to internal-state geometry, collective quantum electromagnetic responses, material currents, and the complete stress–energy tensor of a relativistic scalar field. It distinguishes the information contained in a joint source state from the information accessible through a particular coupling, including collective bright and dark responses that cannot be recovered from separate local states alone. In the gravitational calculations, two internal phase arrangements with matching initial local current, stress, and geometry subsequently produce different neutral-probe tidal responses. A specified optical construction carries a selected difference into receiver-clock intervals, radar distance, and interference signals. The response persists in an independently solved zero-charge family, demonstrating that an electromagnetic source field is not required for this particular modelled gravitational phase dependence. The paper also establishes a restricted mathematical connection between the programme’s nested gravitational source proposal and conventional field stress. An amplitude-weighted cosine expression appears as the equal-amplitude, single-component limit of a squared transported field difference. Retaining amplitude variation, internal-state overlap, and directional and temporal information permits reconstruction of the complete source and its gravitational accounting. Foundational Phase remains nonspatial in the proposed interpretation; coordinates and dynamics belong to the represented coupling description. The results are conditional mathematical correspondences and numerical findings using supplied interactions, Maxwell equations, Einstein gravity, and ideal receiver laws. Physical source identification, dimensional calibration, and measured receiver response remain open. The quantum and classical calculations are separate models, with no quantum-to-classical derivation claimed. The accompanying reproducibility release contains the synthesis, branch master, twenty-one checkpoint reports, original computational packages, and a catalogue linking results to their verification procedures.
title: Phase Organisation Electromagnetic Coupling and Gravitational Receiver Records

summary: When a central bank raises rates, the government's interest bill rises. Whether the extra interest supports domestic demand depends on who receives it. Recent evidence finds this direct fiscal channel of monetary policy was small in the United States before 2020, because long Treasury maturities slowed the pass-through of policy rates to interest costs. We argue that this conclusion does not carry over to the post-2022 tightening. Quantitative easing replaced long-term Treasury debt with overnight interest-bearing reserves, so the consolidated public sector repriced far faster than Treasury maturities suggest, and the price-insensitive official holders that once anchored demand for Treasuries were replaced at the margin by domestic private buyers. Using published Treasury, Federal Reserve and TIC data, we decompose the rise in public-sector interest outflows between 2021 and 2024. Net interest rose by about \$530 billion, three quarters of it due to higher rates rather than more debt. Counting the Treasury and the Federal Reserve together, roughly 57 percent of the increase in public-sector interest outflows reached domestic non-federal holders directly, 27 percent reached them through the Federal Reserve's payments on reserves and reverse repos, whose counterpart was the end of its remittances to the Treasury, and 16 percent went abroad. For the Treasury securities the Federal Reserve held at the end of 2021, quantitative easing made higher rates reach non-federal holders' income roughly two to two and a half times as fast as if the bonds had stayed in private hands. Domestic investors absorbed close to 90 percent of the growth in privately held debt. We discuss what this implies for the potency of rate hikes, for the design of interest on reserves, and for reserve-currency issuers more generally.
title: Who Receives the Interest? Reserve Status, Holder Composition and the Fiscal Channel of Monetary Policy

summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.
title: AETHER-64: High-Throughput Binary Devirtualization via Bit-Parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction and SSA Bytecode Promotion

summary: The work builds a foundation of physics from a single assumption: everything is a process, and a process is an ideal sine; its centre, the balance, is the observer. Only the square — intensity without phase — passes between levels; from this arise dimensions, the arrow of time, the quantum and the standard. On this basis stable particles are built as standing waves together with their galactic analogues, the initial rules of quantum mechanics and relativity are derived, and the constants are linked to a single number — the speed of light. Agreement with experiment is at the level of a few percent; the model attributes the discrepancies to the imperfection of the standard. Main results The four stable particles (neutrino, electron, neutron, proton) are the four stable states of a standing wave; masses from the speed of light alone: electron +0.7 %, nucleons about −3 % [result given hypotheses]. The Born rule, the randomness of a single outcome, the 2√2 limit in the Bell test, spin ½ and g = 2 [result]. The Lorentz transformation from the “speed budget” c² = v² + v_int², the Klein — Gordon and Schrödinger equations, Schwarzschild gravitational time dilation and the light deflection of 1.75″ [result]. Similarity of the small and the large with the step c⁴: the image of the neutron is the stellar mass of the Milky Way (5.5·10¹⁰ versus (6.1 ± 1.1)·10¹⁰ solar masses) [hypothesis, numerical agreement]. The large end is built by the same logic as the microworld: the construction yields the Hubble constant H₀ = 1/(5c²) ≈ 68.7 km/s/Mpc and the smallest acceleration of galaxies a₀ = 1/(10πc) [result given hypotheses]. The gravitational constant G ≈ c^(−6/5) (0.8 %); the mass of the Universe and the scale of dark energy are expressed through c [hypothesis]. The fine-structure constant has been found as the number 1/α ≈ 4·(c/2π)^(1/5) (0.22 %); its meaning is open [observation]. Limitations: the accuracy is percent-level, not parts per million; the standard and several constants remain open questions. The status of each statement is given in the text. Revision dated 2026-10-24:   The black hole. A black hole is understood as the construction of mass from the large end: particles build mass from the small end, the black hole from the large one. Perception has a limit of tempo: a process whose tempo is below our smallest does not change for us, so the centre is inaccessible, and for us it is space possessing mass and rotation. The horizon is the transition from space into mass; it grows with mass and is not related to the core. The black hole processes volumetric particles into a plane, and the tension of space, when the sizes of galaxies change, again gives birth to particle–antiparticle pairs: the cycle is closed. Only black holes that are analogues of elementary particles are considered. G and α. Both constants have received a geometric reading. Gravity is the work of space in a cross-section, charge is the same work over a closed surface; the surface of a sphere is four times its cross-section, hence the four. Charge is the work of one unpaired half-wave, that is, of one step of the microworld k: 1/α = 4k. G is gravity from the large end: the whole linear path up to the transition and the step linking it with the small end, G = 1/(c·c^(1/5)), without the four. The link of the two constants is G = 4α/((2π)^(1/5)·c). In neutral particles the same transition from flat to volume goes through rotation (support: the magnetic moment of the neutron). The residuals of 0.22 % in α and 0.8 % in G are not yet explained.       Работа строит основу физики из одного допущения: всё — процесс, а процесс — идеальный синус; его центр, баланс, — наблюдатель. Между уровнями проходит только квадрат — интенсивност
title: The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton

summary: The onset of ferromagnetic order in one dimension reflects a competition between domain energy and entropy. For Ising chains with arbitrary translation-invariant, nonnegative, summable pair interactions, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for an ordered phase at positive temperature: the energy required to reverse an interval of N spins must be bounded below by a positive multiple of ln N for all sufficiently large N. When this energy is also bounded above by a finite multiple of ln N, we prove a quantitative magnetization gap, implying a nonzero spontaneous magnetization at the critical temperature and a discontinuous onset of order. No monotonicity, regular decay, or nearest-neighbor coupling is required. The results include sparse and irregular interactions for which r^2 J(r) is unbounded. Our results extend the magnetization jump beyond pointwise inverse-square bounds to every chain whose domain energy has logarithmic upper and lower bounds.
title: Onset of Ferromagnetic Order in Ising Chains

summary: This study presents a comprehensive analysis integrating archaeological evidence with modelled radiocarbon dating, isotopic data, and organic residue analysis, offering new insights into prehistoric funerary practices in south-eastern Europe, as exemplified by burial mound number 3 at Mogila, Bulgaria. The mound contained twelve graves, including eleven inhumations and one cremation. The primary chronological classification of the inhumations was based on burial rites and body positions, assigning them to the Early Bronze Age and Middle/Late Bronze Age. Together with a shallowly deposited cremation dated to the Iron Age, three main phases of mound use were identified. Radiocarbon dating enabled the refinement of these phases allowing a detailed reconstruction of the mound’s chronological development and the identification of successive sequences of burial deposition within each period. It also allowed for the chronological attribution of two disarticulated burials. Stable carbon (δ¹³C) and nitrogen (δ¹⁵N) isotope values of the buried individuals revealed similarities within sub-phases of the Early Bronze Age and Middle/Late Bronze Age, as well as dietary differences between individuals from the two periods. In addition, a clay vessel from Middle/Late Bronze Age grave number 10 complemented the isotopic results, indicating the presence of animal lipids, most likely dairy fats.
title: The Long Life of a Burial Mound at Mogila, Bulgaria: From the Bronze Age to the Iron Age

summary: For a finite connected graph $G$, let $e(G)$ be the exponent of its Jacobian and $\Delta(G)$ its maximum degree. For each integer $b\ge1$, the simple biconnected graphs with $e(G)\le b$ form finitely many isomorphism classes if and only if $b\le7$; exactly eleven occur with $e(G)\le7$. The simple biconnected graphs with $e(G)-\Delta(G)\le3$ are $K_n$ ($n\ge3$), $C_4$, $C_5$ and $K_{2,3}$. At exponent eight, the number of vertices is unbounded among simple planar bipartite biconnected graphs of maximum degree four. For every integer $r\ge1$, there is a simple planar biconnected graph whose Jacobian is isomorphic to $(\mathbb Z/8\mathbb Z)^r$, with explicit divisor generators and an orthogonal decomposition of its monodromy pairing. Every simple $3$-connected planar graph satisfies $2|V(G)|-4\le(e(G)-\Delta(G)+1)^2$ and $2|V(G)|-5\le3e(G)^2/5$. Every simple graph with a cellular torus embedding whose full inverse image in the universal cover of the torus is $3$-connected satisfies $|V(G)|\le e(G)^2$. MSC 2020: 05C25, 05C50, 05C10, 05C40, 20K01.
title: Finiteness thresholds and surface bounds for graph Jacobians

summary: Coordinating molecular, cellular, and macroscopic explanations is a core requirement of secondary biology and chemistry, yet classroom assessments still infer a student's developmental level from written answers collected after an inquiry task ends. Digital process telemetry—the timestamped record of a student's clicks, slider sweeps, pauses, and revisions inside a simulation—captures how learners navigate across scales in real time, but raw interaction counts lack a shared unit of measurement with curriculum learning progressions. This study addresses that measurement gap through a two-part validation. First, a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of 86 studies (312 effect sizes; 48,920 learners) synthesized cross-scale inquiry interventions and yielded a pooled Hedges' g of 0.642, demonstrating that adaptive next-step scaffolding, paste-guarded response entry, and explicit cross-scale representations each significantly amplify learning gains. Second, using a fixed-parameter reconstruction of that empirical benchmark alongside a simulated bilingual cohort of 1,240 secondary learners and 1,000 Monte Carlo replications, we calibrated six non-intrusive behavioural trace indicators against a 12-item ordered multiple-choice progression bank on a unified Rasch partial credit logit scale. Common-scale linking error was 0.118 logits (10.9% of the critical Level 2–3 transition interval). Trace-based classifications reproduced item-based progression levels with 81.45% accuracy and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient of .768, exhibited strict measurement invariance across language tracks, gender, and prior achievement, and confirmed that genuine self-regulatory behaviours rather than interface guardrails drive diagnostic classification. Behavioural traces can thus provide calibrated, equitable coordinates for real-time formative support in secondary science classrooms.
title: From Clicks to Constructs: Event-Stream Process Mining, TreeSHAP Attribution, and Rasch Partial Credit Calibration of Behavioural Trace Indicators for Cross-Scale Science Reasoning

summary: Supplementary methods, results, data tables and analysis code for the manuscript Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity. The five resources contain supplementary methods, tables and figures, detailed data workbooks, reproducibility code and supporting audit documentation. Original code is licensed under MIT; original documentation and derived content are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party materials retain their source terms; see LICENSES.md and source notices inside Online_Resource_3.zip. Manuscript abstract Public intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) datasets cover different tissue compartments and measure different subsets of genes, complicating comparisons across studies. We compared four specified gene sets (inflammation, complement, microglial activation and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-associated oxidative stress) in public paired human brain, single-cell and hematoma-effluent/blood datasets, using patients rather than cells as inferential units. In two studies of paired brain tissue, inflammation, complement and NRF2-associated scores were higher in perihematomal than contralateral samples in all four patient blocks and five matched pairs. Patient-level single-cell comparisons found higher inflammatory and complement scores in microglia/monocyte groups than in comparator lineages. In 14 patients with same-hour paired CD14+ and neutrophil data, a five-gene score named for microglial activation showed a positive CD14+–neutrophil local-response interaction in all 14 (adjusted P=0.000488), but four-program heterogeneity was not established (Friedman P=0.0796). Restricting this score to three shared genes reversed its CD14+ local response; a jointly scaled three-gene interaction was near zero. Independent acute blood data showed positive case-control differences, whereas longitudinal changes were not significant after adjustment. Inflammatory and NRF2-associated expression differences recurred across these datasets. The CD14+ local response of the microglial-related score depended on its measured genes. Version 2026-10-24 changes This revision aligns the five supplementary resources with the current manuscript and adds the exact GSE163256 primary fractional-count-to-score reconstruction and fresh-score downstream verification. Earlier domain-score displays in Online Resource 2, worksheets 05 and 06, are replaced by the fixed-program paired-brain results already used in the manuscript. Superseded, undocumented competitive-null fields are removed from the current Puy13 summary display and export; the defined manufacturer-panel-matched analysis is retained. Scoring and provenance descriptions, archive entry points, fonts, table formatting and numerical display precision have also been corrected. The primary biological scores and current inferential statistics are unchanged. Earlier inputs and execution records are retained with their historical roles identified.
title: Reproducibility materials for Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity

summary: This Zenodo record accompanies the paper “Scalable Measurement-Based Quantum Simulation Patterns for Benchmarking” arXiv.2605.12502   and provides QPatLib v1.0 measurement-pattern datasets in human-readable JSONL together with a ZIP archive of OpenQASM 3.0 circuits used for validation and reproducibility.  The patterns and circuits implement Pauli string unitaries  for benchmark cases.  Cases include all possible string combinations for less than 6 qubits and strings used in Hamiltonians for certain diatomic molecules for 6 or more qubits.     Format:  Each  pattern_*.jsonl file is containins measurement patterns for all subsets for a given model/instance and subset strategy: it begins with a preamble containing model metadata, subset definitions, provenance, and (when feasible) full-pattern test results, followed by one pattern entry per subset. Each subset entry includes a required  pattern_ascii field storing the measurement pattern in the measurement-calculus/Graphix standard with signal shifting, written left-to-right in the canonical order nodes → edges → measurements (with signal dependencies) → byproduct corrections (X/Z). The circuits are included as circuit_files.zip.   Patterns in this record were validated against the corresponding circuits and checked for causal flow.   Codes for generating these patterns can be found at QPatLib repository on Github

summary: Overview This repository contains the replication data, source code, execution logs, and complete analytical outputs for the study: “Detectability of controlled leaks in an Andean water transmission main: a field evaluation of changepoint methods on flow and pressure signals.” The study evaluates the detectability of short-duration controlled leaks using five changepoint and anomaly-detection approaches applied to 30-second flow and pressure measurements collected during two field campaigns in an operational water transmission main in Loja, Ecuador. The evaluated methods are: Pruned Exact Linear Time using the Bayesian Information Criterion (PELT-BIC), Pruned Exact Linear Time using the Akaike Information Criterion (PELT-AIC), Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection (BOCD), Cumulative Sum control charts (CUSUM), Moving-average ±3σ control-chart baseline. The repository contains the complete workflow used to: verify field records and ground-truth leak timings; perform campaign-specific spectral analyses using multitaper estimation; evaluate changepoint-detection performance; quantify event-level leak detectability; compare observed performance against chance-level expectations; assess BOCD sensitivity to hazard-rate and threshold settings; generate precision-recall curves and average-precision statistics; perform cross-campaign validation analyses; estimate theoretical detection-delay bounds for flow-based detection. This version supersedes earlier releases by correcting changepoint-index alignment, revising false-alarm-rate calculations using exposure time outside detection windows, replacing pooled spectral analyses with campaign-specific multitaper analyses, and incorporating event-level detectability, chance-level benchmarking, precision-recall evaluation, cross-campaign validation, and theoretical detection-delay analyses. Dataset Description The repository is organized into raw data files and compressed archives containing the complete computational environment and analytical outputs. 1. summary: After more than a decade of development, high-resolution spectroscopy plays a central role in the atmospheric characterization of exoplanets, offering insights into planetary chemical composition, thermal structure, and atmospheric dynamics. Among the most intriguing targets for atmospheric characterization are Ultra-Hot Jupiters (UHJs), which, due to their extreme temperatures and intense stellar irradiation, serve as unique laboratories for studying planetary atmospheres under extreme conditions. In this talk, I will discuss what we can learn and what challenges we must confront when interpreting high-resolution observations of UHJs, using KELT-9b (equilibrium temperature ~4000 K) as a benchmark case. Based on transmission and emission observations obtained with the near-infrared spectrograph GIANO-B at the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo (TNG), I explore how different modeling assumptions impact the detectability and interpretation of atmospheric signals. In particular, the extreme irradiation conditions of these planets may give rise to departures from local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), making non-LTE effects potentially non-negligible. At the same time, the strong day–night temperature contrasts and asymmetric terminator regions expected in UHJs challenge the applicability of 1D atmospheric models, which may lead to biased or incomplete interpretations of the observed signals.   These effects can have important consequences for the inferred atmospheric abundances and bias the interpretation of key quantities such as the C/O and R/H ratios, which are used to constrain planetary formation and evolutionary scenarios. Addressing these challenges is therefore crucial to robustly link high-resolution observations of UHJs to their origins.
title: INTERPRETING EXTREME ATMOSPHERES: Lessons from High-Resolution spectroscopy of an Ultra-Hot Jupiter

summary: The spectroscopic analysis of cool dwarfs (T_eff < 4700 K) is challenging due to their low effective temperatures, which produce complex spectra dominated by dense molecular absorption bands. These challenges have limited the availability of accurate and homogeneous chemical abundance measurements for these stars. To address these difficulties, we developed AutoSpecFit (ASF) , an automated, line-by-line synthetic spectral fitting code, together with AutoSpecNorm (ASN) , a complementary code designed to perform local pseudo-continuum normalization of observed and synthetic spectra. The combined ASF+ASN framework enables detailed chemical abundance analysis of cool dwarfs using high-resolution optical and near-infrared spectra. ASF employs multiple χ² minimization procedures and iterative optimization to account for the complex correlations among elemental abundances. ASN independently normalizes each synthetic spectrum, ensuring consistent comparisons with observations and reducing uncertainties associated with continuum placement in molecularly crowded spectral regions. Version 2.0 extends the original abundance-fitting framework by introducing an iterative procedure that alternates between the determination of stellar atmospheric parameters and elemental abundances. This approach accounts for the interdependencies between atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances, while employing selected diagnostic spectral lines and iterative optimization to mitigate parameter degeneracies and achieve a self-consistent solution. The updated methodology has been applied to benchmark M dwarfs with independently determined stellar properties, providing an opportunity to evaluate the reliability and consistency of the derived atmospheric parameters and elemental abundances. The ASF+ASN framework has been developed to measure the abundances of up to 15 key elements in cool dwarfs, including major planet-building elements such as C, O, Mg, Si, and Fe. These measurements provide essential constraints on the chemical compositions of exoplanetary systems and their formation and evolution. Furthermore, the application of this framework to metal-poor cool dwarfs offers opportunities to investigate the chemical enrichment history, structure, and evolution of the Milky Way.
title: Detailed Abundance Measurements of Cool Dwarfs: Prospects for Exploring the Galaxy from Stellar Populations to Star-Planet Chemical Connections

summary: HBB2OBB converts horizontal (axis-aligned) bounding boxes (HBBs) into oriented (rotated) bounding boxes (OBBs) by using existing HBB annotations as prompts for segmentation models from the SAM (Segment Anything Model) family. It targets object detection tasks where objects appear at arbitrary orientations, such as aerial imagery, satellite data, and traffic monitoring, producing oriented boxes that tightly encapsulate non-upright objects without any re-annotation. Beyond conversion, it provides horizontal box detection, evaluation, hyperparameter optimization, an interactive annotation viewer, and annotation format-conversion tools, exposed through both a command-line interface and a Python API. 📖 Documentation: rfonod.github.io/hbb2obb , with a quick start on the bundled sample data, a guide per command, pages on how the conversion works, the confidence score, the metrics and provenance, and a CLI and API reference generated from the code. Why HBB2OBB 🎯 Accurate OBBs from HBBs : prompts SAM-family segmentation models with existing horizontal boxes to fit tight oriented boxes around non-upright objects, with no re-annotation required. 🚗 No HBBs? Detect them : the hbb2obb-detect command runs an Ultralytics detector over the images and writes the horizontal boxes the conversion consumes, confidence column included. 🧩 Model ensemble : combines masks from multiple SAM variants through majority voting for more robust, accurate results. 🛡️ Spatially constrained and safe : region-specific masking and contour refinement keep segmentation inside the object, a mask split by an occluder is fitted back together, and a fallback retains the original HBB when no valid mask is found, counted and reported rather than left to be discovered afterwards. 🔎 Confidence-scored output : every OBB receives a heuristic quality score in [0, 1] that flags silent fallbacks and low-confidence conversions, so you know which boxes to trust; the scores go in the label files or in a side-car directory that keeps them strictly standard, and the detector's own confidence can be carried through instead of, or on top of, that score. 📐 Flexible scaling : positive or negative scale factors, optionally different for the short and long sides, recover cropped object parts or tighten overly conservative annotations. 📊 Evaluate and optimize : evaluation against ground truth on IoU, orientation error, and the share of boxes above a high IoU bar, plus the hbb2obb-optimize command, a hyperparameter search over SAM inference resolution, scale factors, and morphological opening kernel, driven by a configuration file so that a whole benchmark of model ensembles is a single reproducible command. 🔬 Where the score comes from : the hbb2obb-analyze command breaks one evaluation down by the ground truth's orientation, size, frame edge, difficulty and class, and scores the conversion against emitting the horizontal prompt unchanged. 🔄 Five annotation formats : read and write YOLO, DOTA, Pascal VOC, COCO, and LabelMe, for horizontal and oriented boxes alike, with a check that proves every format encodes the same boxes. 🔍 Interactive viewer : the hbb2obb-view command pans and zooms over the annotations, in any format, coloring boxes by confidence and overlaying predictions against ground truth. Where a set ships the same boxes several ways, it names the format on screen and switches between them on a keypress. Features HBB to OBB conversion of YOLO-format annotations using SAM-based segmentation, written in absolute pixels or, with --normalize , relative to [0, 1], the convention Ultralytics reads. HBB detection : produce the horizontal boxes in the first place with any Ultralytics detector, a local file, a link, the Ultralytics catalogue, or Hugging Face, passing any other predictor argument straight through. Multiple model support : SAM, SAM2, SAM2.1, SAM3, Mobile SAM, and FastSAM families. Model ensemble via majority voting for enhanced accuracy. Confidence scoring : a per-OBB quali
title: HBB2OBB: Horizontal to Oriented Bounding Box Conversion and Evaluation Tool

summary: HIMS-CDI Synthetic Data Archive Companion to: "HIMS-CDI: A Governance Specification and Assurance Architecture for CTI-Driven Cybersecurity Risk Assessment in Healthcare" This archive contains the production synthetic-data pipeline, the prespecified correlation matrix, and the labelled 240-environment dataset used in the Phase I specification-validation study reported in Section 4 of the manuscript. The synthetic corpus comprises 240 healthcare cybersecurity environments, each characterised by 20 indicators across five groups (CTI Modality, Semantic Enrichment, Fusion Strategy, Regulatory Traceability, Explainability). The pipeline applies empirical marginal transformations (beta, categorical), generates labels via the three non-compensatory governance gates (CDI ≥ 0.70, CCR ≥ 0.80, latency < 200 ms, memory < 100 MB), injects Gaussian noise (σ = 0.13), and performs a stratified 60/20/20 split (seed 123). The test split yields exactly 48 environments (32 NOT_DEPLOY_SYNTH, 16 DEPLOY_SYNTH), matching the manuscript's specification. Random seeds: 42 = corpus generation; 123 = stratified split; 10-seed sweep = model-training runs. Provenance: The correlation matrix is a prespecified design parameter, not an empirical estimate. MITRE ATT&CK v14.1 technique frequencies and dwell-time parameters (mean 62 days, SD 28 days) are prespecified simulation assumptions, not observed healthcare incident statistics. Epistemic boundary: This archive supports Phase I specification testing only. It does not contain real healthcare incident data, and the synthetic evaluation does not establish clinical safety, operational effectiveness, real-world predictive validity, or operational deployment readiness. Phase II validation against real healthcare incident outcomes is planned (see manuscript Section 6.2–6.3).
title: HIMS-CDI Synthetic Data Archive

summary: BIODEGRADABLE NANOROBOT MANUFACTURING AND LIFECYCLE ENGINEERING AT THE LIMIT Biodegradable Materials x Functional Manufacturing x Degradation Kinetics This high-density English research monograph develops a falsification-oriented architecture for manufacturing biodegradable biomedical nano- and microrobots whose functional lifetime and terminal fate can be jointly qualified. Its central problem is a dual-clock constraint: the device must preserve propulsion, structure and interface function throughout a declared mission, then degrade or be retrieved within a separate terminal window without leaving unidentified or high-risk residues. The volume refuses to treat in-vitro weight loss as biological clearance. Hydrolysis, molecular-weight reduction, erosion, dissolution, fragmentation, adsorption, retrieval, magnetic-core persistence, biological transformation and safe elimination are defined as distinct measurable states. A five-compartment ledger preserves solid mass, soluble products, fragments, recovered material and unexplained residual; the last category is never presumed safe. The monograph contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 independently paginated section studies, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Formula plates state variables, units, assumptions, identifiability, specific blind falsification tests and chapter interfaces. Research Gates specify complete-denominator protocols, analytical evidence, competing explanations, hard stops and successor forks.

summary: Resolution Geometry: A Kernel–Stabilizer Geometry of Observability Abstract Resolution Geometry (RG) is a protocol-explicit framework for characterizing what a declared observation system can distinguish, preserve, and consistently infer. Its starting point is a family of observation laws together with admissible outcome relabelings, rather than a covariance decomposition, metric, or dynamical model. Equality of the joint observation law defines a kernel groupoid and an observational quotient, canonically identified with the law image. An experiment-internal quantity is identifiable precisely when it is constant on observational fibres. The quotient alone determines neither a metric nor a connection, causal structure, clock, physical scale, or law of motion. The framework separates exact observational equivalence from statistical distinguishability, admissibility, symmetry, and physical realization. The stabilizer of the observation law induces a faithful effective action on the quotient. Liftable symmetry is distinguished from symmetry of the law image: the former can depend on the latent presentation, whereas the observable layer is presentation-invariant once its law-space structures and declarations are fixed. On regular strata, natural modules defined by pullback from law space descend uniquely to the observational quotient. This gives representative independence and projectability for law-defined structures, without asserting that naturality selects those structures. In regular classical experiments, the Fisher tensor supplies infinitesimal distinguishability under the stated Markov-monotonicity assumptions; its radical agrees with the observational vertical space under the corresponding regularity conditions. Quantum protocols require a declared operational task to select within the family of monotone metrics. A central organizing result concerns task-preserving conversion . For a representation map and a declared family of downstream tasks, RG characterizes the exact set of compatible task outcomes on each representation fibre. Unique inference is possible exactly when this residual is a singleton. Otherwise the appropriate output is a correspondence or a typed abstention, not an arbitrary hidden representative. Pairing a representation with its tasks gives a terminal sufficient refinement. For declared operations, observational closure is expressed by the greatest operation-stable congruence contained in the observation kernel. These constructions distinguish local differential rank, global orbit separation, observational completeness, and reconstruction, and make preservation requirements explicit under composition. Second-order realizations provide concrete classification and computational tools. Under a declared block-orthogonal gauge, a covariance datum is encoded by a symmetric matrix tuple whose ordered word traces form a complete pointwise invariant, including repeated eigenvalues, vanishing couplings, and rank-deficient sectors. On simple-spectrum strata, mixed moments recover coupling magnitudes, while independent cycle holonomies complete the residual sign classification. This distinguishes hidden values omitted by a descriptor from distinctions that are genuinely observationally null . Under the different contract of covariance-preserving block-linear transformations, canonical correlations with multiplicity classify pointwise data; constant-type families additionally carry bundle and gluing information. Pointwise classification therefore does not replace the transport, relative alignment, or global data required by field-level tasks. Across rank, symmetry, and protocol changes, RG uses specialization maps when kernel inclusion permits them and correspondences otherwise. Smooth geometry is confined to its regular domain; proper-groupoid and tame settings support stratified descriptions with slices, tangent cones, and orbit-type changes. Finite-resolution statements are separated from exact model state
title: Resolution Geometry of Observation Systems

summary: PRECISION NANOROBOTIC DRUG CARRIER MANUFACTURING AND QUALITY CONTROL AT THE LIMIT Drug Carriers x Precision Manufacturing x Quality Metrology This high-density English research monograph develops a falsification-oriented architecture for joint batch assurance of precision nanorobotic drug carriers. Its central rule is that attractive marginal averages do not constitute a qualified lot. Particle-size tails, manufactured and biofluid-transformed surface identity, true payload localization, release kinetics, residues and analytical visibility must be measured on representative units from the same unselected batch and adjudicated with their covariance intact. The volume treats the manufacturing process and the measurement system as two coupled sources of risk. Microfluidic mixing time, nucleation, residence-time distribution, fouling, raw-material variation and tenfold scale-up are challenged alongside detector saturation, weighting conversion, dilution artifacts, separation recovery and convenience sampling. A process is not accepted when the analytical chain cannot see the defect it is expected to exclude. The monograph contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 independently paginated section studies, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 genuinely distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. Every Gate begins with a large deep-navy bold question and continues with a blind protocol, evidence package, competing explanation, hard stop and successor fork. The central evidence object is the Carrier Quality Provenance Matrix. It binds raw-material identity, mixer geometry, delivered flows, collection time, sampling inclusion probabilities, raw analytical signals, size and interface distributions, payload mass closure, release curves, storage history and release vetoes. It preserves failed runs and abstentions rather than allowing successful aliquots to redefine the lot.
