summary: NANOSENSING ACUPUNCTURE AND ACUPOINT MICROENVIRONMENT METROLOGY AT THE LIMIT STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW EPOCH / 33 x STARLI ORIGINAL CIVILIZATIONAL INTERPRETATION This English-language prospective research monograph asks whether historically nominated acupuncture points exhibit reproducible paired differences in local electrical impedance or optically inferred superficial tissue oxygenation when compared with anatomically and environmentally matched nonpoint sites. Its core three-coupling is Acupoint Microenvironments x Multimodal Metrology x Paired Control. The principal White Rainbow Epoch Hypothesis is deliberately vulnerable to refutation: analysts blinded to point identity must be able to reconstruct an independently calibrated advantage when equally hydrated measurement sites are exchanged under a concealed test condition. Skin water content, contact pressure, temperature, electrode polarization, ordinary neurovascular anatomy, skin pigmentation, photon pathlength and site-selection bias are treated as strong competing explanations, not minor caveats. The civilizational purpose follows a governing three-coupling: Continuity of Chinese Cultural Heritage x Exploration through Modern Science x Original Civilizational Interpretation of the White Rainbow Epoch. Classical acupuncture, Chinese medical philosophy, yin-yang, Five Phases and Daoist thought are welcomed as inherited cultural frameworks capable of generating questions. They are not relabelled novel SI-measurable energy fields or independently validated clinical mechanisms. Established physical laws and metrological statistics likewise remain inherited knowledge rather than purported discoveries by 33 x STARLI. Newly composed, falsifiable interdisciplinary proposals are marked White Rainbow Epoch Hypotheses. Cultural interpretation may remain meaningful even when a particular physical hypothesis fails. The book contains 30 mechanism-distinct golden mathematical plates, 82 scientific chapters and 410 individually paginated research investigations, 200 one-page Research Gates whose large deep-navy opening questions lead to discriminating experiments, and 33 scientifically distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. The plates include complex impedance, electrode polarization, pressure and hydration sensitivity, optical pathlength, chromophore inversion, heat transport, oxygen diffusion, spatial statistics, hierarchical and covariance-aware inference, multiplicity, null-equivalence and hard integrity vetoes. The Gates present concrete blinded challenges, resource-matched traditional metrology baselines, necessary calibration and acceptance margins, failure pathways and independent handoff requirements. Each Phoenix embryo has a different named instrument or provisional mechanism, adversarial test, rival explanation and honest metamorphosis path when rejected. The editorial DOI scope is intentionally limited to three author-associated STARLI mother research volumes: 10.5281/zenodo.23480803 (AI Microrobotic Sensing of Senescent-Cell Heterogeneity at the Limit), 10.5281/zenodo.23486020 (Reconfigurable Robotic Swarms and Continuous Functional Regeneration at the Limit), and 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 (Microrobotic Sampling and Quantum Biosensing Co-Design at the Limit). Their chapter lineages offer methodological ancestry in measurement provenance, bias governance, independent requalification and sample-state preservation. They are not independent evidence that the proposed acupoint effect exists. The project does not exclude established scientific knowledge or ancient philosophy; it simply does not include other authors' DOI records in this particular bibliography.

summary: INTELLIGENT NANO-ACUPUNCTURE AND CLOSED-LOOP NEUROMODULATION AT THE LIMIT White Rainbow Epoch / 33 × STARLI Original Civilizational Interpretation A Research Flagship in the STARLI White Rainbow Scientific Library ENGLISH DESCRIPTION This prospective research monograph investigates a sharply bounded engineering question: can nanosensing-inspired instrument interfaces and closed-loop neural feedback produce a measurable improvement in feedback latency and electromyographic outcomes when confronted with blinded false-feedback inputs, sensor disconnection, equal-resource conventional controls and independently verified hard-stop conditions? summary: This conceptual theory-building paper develops an interdisciplinary framework for understanding cancer as a model-admissible, potentially persistent system state emerging within complex adaptive biological systems. Building upon evolutionary oncology, dynamical systems theory, cancer-attractor research, tumor plasticity, and adaptive therapy, the study examines how malignant cellular populations may achieve conditional persistence through feedback, selection, environmental constraints, and adaptive reorganization. The central proposition distinguishes biological possibility, dynamical stability, and clinical desirability. Cancer is not described as beneficial or universally stable, but as a pathological configuration whose emergence and persistence may be investigated through formal systems models. The paper integrates three author-developed research architectures: the Akarkach Seven-Stage Emergence Model (A7SEM), A7SEM Reverse, and Pre-Inference Governance Architecture (PIGA). A7SEM provides seven interacting analytical dimensions for studying emergent configurations across biological systems. A7SEM Reverse examines counterhypotheses, contradictory evidence, dependency structures, and falsifiability. PIGA separates the admission of scientific inferences from authorization for consequential actions. Four testable research hypotheses, competing explanations, mathematical templates, and falsification criteria are presented. The framework is further connected to artificial intelligence through structural comparisons involving emergence, uncertainty, observability, and system governance. The study extends the theoretical foundations of the monograph Cancer as a Legitimate System State and connects related publications within the Faith Poetry Research Series. Its principal contribution is an integrated evolutionary, systems-theoretical, and epistemic framework for investigating malignant persistence without conflating mathematical coherence with empirical confirmation or clinical validity. This publication presents theoretical research and a proposed empirical research agenda. It does not establish a validated clinical prediction model, diagnostic procedure, or cancer treatment.
tags: Cancer as a Legitimate System State
title: Cancer as a Legitimate System State: Attractor Dynamics, Evolutionary Plasticity, and Epistemic Governance in Oncology

summary: Here I show my solution to the Hodge Conjecture using my framework and ansatz formulation. The paper starts in 1D, from a simple sieve in mod 9 to a continuum projection, then from a 2D variety in mod 9k, to a continuum projection in 2D which can be map to any elliptic curve with Hasse-Weil operator, doing it back and forward with the inverse operator, linking elliptic curves with continuum topologies or fluid fields, and discovering that the Hasse-Weil function can be the filter we need to detect anomalies, this can allow us to extend this framework to higher dimensions with the master ansatz in 3D.
title: Discrete-Continuum Topology and the Hodge Conjecture: A Compressible Maxwell-Navier-Stokes and Modulo-9 Sieve Framework

summary: Highlights of the Study This comprehensive review examines the fatigue behaviour of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds , addressing a critical but comparatively underexplored aspect of bone tissue engineering. It evaluates the mechanisms governing fatigue damage and systematically examines how polymer characteristics, microstructure, reinforcing materials, scaffold topology, manufacturing methods, loading conditions, body fluids, and tissue ingrowth influence fatigue performance, with particular emphasis on translating polymeric scaffolds toward reliable load-bearing clinical applications. Key findings: 🟢 Fatigue failure mechanisms: Polymeric scaffolds can undergo both mechanical and thermal fatigue. Repeated cyclic loading causes residual-strain accumulation, stiffness and peak-stress reduction, crack development, and hysteretic heating, which can progressively degrade polymer chains and ultimately cause structural failure. 🟢 Low- and high-cycle fatigue: Low-cycle fatigue generally occurs under relatively high stresses and involves repeated plastic deformation, whereas high-cycle fatigue develops over much larger numbers of cycles under lower stress levels and is primarily associated with elastic deformation and progressive material degradation. 🟢 Material and microstructural effects: Polymer fatigue resistance is strongly governed by molecular and microstructural characteristics. Increased crystallinity, molecular weight, and molecular-chain entanglement can improve fatigue resistance, emphasizing the importance of selecting and tailoring the polymer microstructure for load-bearing scaffolds. 🟢 Reinforcement strategy: Incorporating ceramic or metallic reinforcing phases can substantially improve the fatigue performance of polymeric scaffolds by redistributing applied loads and dissipating energy that would otherwise contribute to polymer deformation and heat generation. 🟢 Hydroxyapatite reinforcement: Incorporation of 15 wt% hydroxyapatite increased the fatigue limit of PLA scaffolds by approximately 17%, while also improving compressive modulus, crack resistance, and hysteresis energy compared with unreinforced PLA. 🟢 Scaffold topology: Pore architecture plays a decisive role in fatigue behaviour by controlling stress distribution and stress concentration. Even scaffolds fabricated from the same polymer and having comparable porosity can exhibit substantially different fatigue lives when their pore geometry and filament arrangement are changed. 🟢 Topology-dependent fatigue life: Among 3D-printed PLA scaffolds with comparable porosity, the tetragonal topology achieved a fatigue life of approximately 4400 cycles, outperforming hexagonal and wheel-like structures at approximately 3200 and 2500 cycles, respectively. 🟢 Advanced scaffold architectures: TPMS, Voronoi, functionally graded, auxetic, and other irregular architectures offer promising approaches for load-bearing scaffolds. TPMS structures are particularly attractive because their smooth transitions at strut junctions may reduce stress concentrations, although their polymer fatigue behaviour remains insufficiently investigated. 🟢 Bone-inspired architecture: Bio-inspired scaffold design can substantially improve fatigue performance. Increasing the thickness of transverse rod-like struts in bone-inspired structures was reported to enhance fatigue life by approximately 10–100 times with relatively minor effects on density and stiffness. 🟢 Porosity–strength trade-off: Increasing porosity promotes permeability, vascularization, cell migration, and tissue ingrowth but simultaneously reduces scaffold stiffness, strength, and load-bearing capacity. Therefore, successful scaffold design requires balancing biological benefits against fatigue and mechanical integrity. 🟢 Stress concentration: Geometrical discontinuities and sharp pore corners create localized stress concentrations that accelerate fatigue damage. Circular pores can provide more uniform stress distribu
title: Fatigue behavior of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds: A review

summary: Related: Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels , accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? Version of record: SSRN 7653679 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7653679 . Cite that version. The same text is also at polyhelper.ai/research/sealed-before-the-open/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/sealed-before-the-open . The registered predictions of Section 8 are on OSF: 10.17605/OSF.IO/9Q86N . The immutable release of the open league files on which every number of the paper rests: 10.5281/zenodo.23552700 . The live league and its open data (CC BY 4.0): trends.polyhelper.ai/markets , trends.polyhelper.ai/api/v1 . This deposit is an archival copy made so that the full text stays retrievable; it makes no separate claim. When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. Check a seal with three commands, and score my thirty predictions, registered on OSF, before I do.
title: Sealed Before the Open: A Verifiable Standard for Measuring AI Forecasts of Financial Markets

summary: Spatial Methods Workbench is a citation-aware R Shiny environment with 12 guided workflows for spatial autocorrelation, conditional networks, spatially adjusted 2D and 3D networks, spatially varying networks, prediction, clustering, image-regression screening, mediation, and statistical shape analysis. Version 0.4.0 re-targets the three advanced network paths to the current public engines. The ISPat 2D and ISPat 3D paths call the CRAN package ISPAT3D 0.3.1 ( ispat3d_fit_2d for the section-wise planar fit and ispat3d_fit for the pooled volumetric fit: Matern-3/2 Vecchia Gaussian-process adjustment on spatially balanced anchors followed by a shared-plus-zone factor covariance fitted by Gaussian maximum likelihood, reported as signed zone partial correlations). The GP-GHS path calls GPGHS 1.0.1 ( gpghs_graph ) with the shrinkage-factor selection rule and AND symmetry of the accompanying article, and returns the GPGHS edge table with scores and signs. The retired ISPAT 0.1.0, ISPAT3D 0.1.1, and GPGHS 0.1.0 interfaces targeted by v0.3.1 no longer exist upstream. New controls expose factor rank, anchor budget, Vecchia neighbors, optimizer iterations, section handling, threads, and seeds; readiness checks require at least two zones with more rows than markers; result manifests record the engine package, version, and function; and real adapter smoke tests run whenever the engines are installed. This complete source distribution contains the installable Workbench package, Shiny application, five executable vignettes, compact simulated datasets, complete documentation, automated checks, and locally bundled package sources for the exact CRAN ISPAT3D 0.3.1 and GPGHS 1.0.1 engines. install-complete.R installs those local engine copies and the single compiled dependency gpboost without cloning their repositories. summary: RASHER begins as a fork of BACoN 0.4.0 (commit 4fdec16, which includes the samtools consensus -C 20 change below), adapted to Illumina short reads. Everything under "BACoN changelog" is the parent tool's history, kept for provenance. Changed Renamed throughout: the package, command, log ( rasher.log ) and lock file ( .rasher.lock ) are rasher . The pipeline reads Illumina short reads , paired or single-end. sample_R1 / sample_R2 , sample_1 / _2 sample.R1 / .R2 and sample.1 / .2 files (bcl2fastq _001 tails included) pair into one sample, in flat folders, subfolders and sample sheets; a file without a mate is a single-end sample, and unmated files next to a sample's pairs are skipped with a warning. A pair is baited whole when either mate matches the reference, mates travel together through every step ( 1_extracted/<sample>_R1/_R2 , 2_filtered/... ), and a desynchronised pair is an error, whether the mates carry identical names or /1 /2 suffixes. Baiting aligns with minimap2 -x sr (BBDuk baits pairs natively with in2= / outm2= ). --keep-bam now keeps the baited reads aligned to the reference (paired samples: a proper paired BAM). Filtering: fastp (adapter trimming, quality and length filters; its JSON and HTML reports land in logs/2_filter/ where MultiQC finds them) followed by deterministic, evenly spread subsampling of the reads (pairs kept whole) to --target-depth . Filtlong, --keep-percent and --filter-by-reference are gone; --min-read-length defaults to 50. Fasta reads skip fastp and are filtered by length. Templated assembly aligns pairs with minimap2 -ax sr and calls samtools consensus -X hiseq (call quality at least 20, as BACoN's unreleased change at the time of the fork). De novo assembly: SKESA ( -a skesa ; the recommended de novo assembler — on the real-data benchmark its SNP distances matched SPAdes' with far fewer contigs) or SPAdes ( -a spades , --isolate ; writes the assembly graph, more robust below ~30x depth). Flye and myloasm are gone, with --read-type and --min-size . --snp-method auto is minimap2 for templated assemblies and SKA2 for SPAdes and SKESA assemblies. -m/--memory also sizes SPAdes and SKESA (it was BBDuk-only). A paired sample X next to a sample named X_R1 or X_R2 is an error (their outputs would collide). No assembler flags circular contigs any more, so SKA2's circular-contig end extension no longer applies. Single-end extraction matches read names with a trailing /1 or /2 stripped, as aligners report them. Output folders of BACoN do not resume under RASHER (the checkpoint fingerprints are seeded with the tool's name; every step runs again); BACoN VCFs are rewritten. Checkpoints record each step's own output signature, and a result is only reused when its output is still the file it wrote: a sample returning to a sheet can no longer pick up reads another sample wrote over. Switching a sample between single-end and paired (or fasta and fastq) removes the other shape's files. BBDuk's paired outputs are checked mate against mate, like minimap2's (a desynchronised pair fails the sample); mates named .1 / .2 ( fastq-dump --readids ) pair; the unpaired-reads file of fasterq-dump --split-3 next to its pair is skipped with a warning; a file cannot pair with a link to itself, and files that look like mates but do not pair are warned about. Stale fastp reports are removed on rerun and for samples that fail at baiting. The report and MultiQC drop the circular-contigs column (no short-read assembler flags circles) and say that read pairs were kept whole when either mate matched.
title: RASHER: Bait, Assemble and Compare Illumina short reads

summary: Entity Matching identifies records that refer to the same real-world entity across one or more data sources. It is a key step in data integration and data cleaning. In practice, real-world datasets are often incomplete, and missing attribute values can significantly reduce the accuracy of traditional and learning-based methods. This presentation introduces a technique that uses Sentence Transformers to address EM under incomplete data. Records are represented as dense semantic embeddings, which allows the approach to capture contextual similarity between tuples even when some attribute values are missing. These embeddings support both the recovery of missing information and the matching of records. Experiments on benchmark datasets with varying levels of missingness show that the approach improves the robustness of entity matching on incomplete data.
title: A Sentence Transformer Based Technique for Entity Matching within Incomplete Data

summary: Background/Objectives : With the advent of the current digital health age, opportunities for interacting with health systems have grown not only more frequent but also variable in type, spanning across emergent care settings, routine outpatient follow-up, as well as at-home telemedicine-based platforms. In light of initiatives to re-design electronic medical records (EMR) to more meaningfully curate evidence-based insights, our research objective is focused on harnessing underutilized data features (i.e., time-ordered events) to map the complex interactions that patients undergo within their health systems. We posit that inclusion of information associated with sequential patterns will help more accurately simulate care pathways and outcomes. We report preliminary data on care utilization patterns among cohorts of patients diagnosed with chronic disease. Methods : De-identified data were extracted from the MedStar Health AIM-AHEAD Data Bridge (AADB)’s Chronic Disease repository. EMRs were queried for patients with confirmed diagnoses for diabetes mellitus (ICD-10: E10.X or E11.X) as well as heart failure (ICD-10: I50.X). For each unique patient, encounters related to care utilization were sequentially collated, with explicit demarcation of whether interactions occurred before or after corresponding diagnoses. For analytical purposes, encounters were categorized as “Emergency”, “Inpatient”, “Observation”, “Outpatient”, “Home Health”, and “Patient Portal”. For each cohort, sequential pattern mining (SPM) was used to generate antecedent-consequent prediction rules and calculate the conditional probabilities (confidence) of subsequent care utilization episodes. Analyses were performed using R (The R Foundation for Statistical Computing; version 4.5.2). Results : Between January 2018 and December 2024, we distinctly identified 202,605 patients with a diagnosis for diabetes mellitus as well as 79,223 patients with a diagnosis for heart failure. Across both cohorts, 42,208 patients had documentation of being diagnosed with both conditions and were flagged separately for potential sensitivity analyses. The proportion of older patients (50 years or above) was predominant (>85% for all patients). The median number of annual healthcare interactions tended to increase post-diagnosis (versus pre-diagnosis) particularly in diabetic cohorts: 3.0 versus 1.0 (diabetes only); 5.0 versus 1.7 (diabetes and heart failure). Total instances of care episodes (t) were enumerated across the 7-year study period: diabetes only (t=3,511,417), heart failure only (t=741,789), diabetes and heart failure (t=1,681,307). SPM algorithms were used to generate rulebooks associating unique care utilization patterns with their corresponding likelihood of subsequent events. Discussion/Conclusions : Our initial findings highlight a wide variability of care utilization patterns among patients diagnosed with chronic diseases. We demonstrated that analyzing care utilization sequences may yield embedded insights that can be harnessed for prospectively tracking person-centered health trajectories. The current work exhibits several limitations and opportunities for expanded analysis. We expect to enrich our data pipeline with more detailed clinical features (e.g., medications, laboratory panels, procedures) in future iterations. This comprehensive ingestion would enable the initial steps towards developing models for predicting the onset of unfavorable health outcomes. Implications: Notwithstanding these considerations, the goals of our preliminary efforts are aligned with learning health systems models which emphasize the implementation of evidence-based insights at the point-of-care. With increasing integration of multi-modal sources of longitudinal health information as well as availability of high-computing resources, connected health technologies may serve as valuable applications from whi
title: Establishing a Scalable Research Reporting Framework for Mapping Healthcare Utilization Trajectories and Outcomes among Chronic Disease Patients Diagnosed with Diabetes and/or Heart Failure

summary: DIGITAL TWINS AND AI CLOSED-LOOP CONTROL FOR NANOROBOTIC PHARMACEUTICAL MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT Digital Twins x AI Process Control x Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Quality This high-density English research monograph develops a falsification-oriented architecture for digital twins and AI closed-loop control in nonclinical nanorobotic pharmaceutical manufacturing research. Its central question is whether a process-state estimator can predict quality failure under raw-material, flow, sensor and equipment drift before the failure occurs, rather than merely replaying historical data as an attractive dashboard. The governing evidence object is the Falsifiable Manufacturing Twin. It binds a declared physical state, observation model, uncertainty envelope, process and sensor versions, candidate and executed control actions, external critical-quality-attribute measurements, abstention, fallback and terminal batch fate. A twin earns authority only while new physical evidence can contradict it. Failed, stopped, out-of-distribution and externally falsified batches remain in the denominator. The monograph compares fixed recipes, statistical process control, tuned PID, strong non-learning model predictive control and AI under equal sensing, energy, constraints and operator access. It treats calibrated ignorance as a successful behavior: an unsupported state must cause abstention, return to a separately qualified safe recipe or stop. External CQA evidence always outranks the model. The volume contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 independently paginated section studies, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 genuinely distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. Every Gate begins with a large deep-navy bold question and continues with a blind protocol, evidence package, competing explanation, hard stop and successor fork.

summary: Meeting the Paris Agreement target and path (PTP) is vital to protect humanity from the worse impacts of global warming. Using a large dimensional and unique Global Trade Analysis Project (GTAP) model for energy and international trade, we calculated the needed change in the energy mix and fall in carbon emissions to meet a minimal PTP of less than 2 o C warming. Covering 30 countries/regions and 31 commodity sectors, the model shows the PTP in annual time steps to 2100 in terms of emissions reduction and the shift in energy mix allowing for changes in energy intensity, renewables growth, and rising carbon prices. By 2050, using a year 2019 baseline, model results show carbon emissions must decrease on a compound basis by at least 5.7% globally, per year, on average, and coal consumption must fall continuously from 2025, complemented by large increases in renewable energy that allow for continued economic growth. We find that global carbon emissions must decline by almost 40% in 2030 and 80% in 2050 to meet a less than 2 o C warming path by 2100. Coal consumption must decline between 85–99% by 2050 among the key emitters (China, the USA, and India), compared to 2019 (the model baseline), complemented by a continuous transition to renewables. For Net-Zero Emissions Targets (NZET), carbon sequestration, such as from re-forestation and land use change, is also essential, although with substantial uncertainty. Model results indicate a net-zero outcome, even with assumed carbon sequestration, occurs no earlier than 2058, at best.

summary: Reproducibility package for Identification Limits in Estimating the Effects of Algorithmic Surveillance on Digital Freedoms. Includes analysis scripts, reference result tables, figures, supplementary material, source-access instructions, software requirements, and verification tools.   Version 1.0.4 (2026-10-24) corrects the copy of the manuscript design figure, figures/Fig1_manuscript.png, whose summary box still stated that standard errors within the supported region are 1.7-3.6 times larger; the cohort-stratified bootstrap introduced in 1.0.3 gives 1.4-2.7, which is what the manuscript reports. That figure is drawn by the authors rather than produced by the pipeline, so the value had not followed the recomputation. The version also updates the expected wordings in scripts/15_audit_manuscript_numbers.py so that the audit tracks the current manuscript text; run against the revised manuscript it reconciles all 460 numerical claims with the archived result files. That audit located one error in the manuscript, which this version documents rather than changes: the last row of Table 7 carried the standard error of the pooled bootstrap, 0.236, where the stratified procedure gives 0.169. No data, code path or result changed; every result table is identical to v1.0.3.   Version 1.0.3 (2026-10-24) responds to the second editorial assessment of the third review round. The bootstrap of the support-restricted subsample is now stratified by adoption cohort with 2,000 replications, replacing pooled resampling of the 34 treated countries with 499: one cohort retains a single treated country and was absent from 191 of the 499 pooled replications, so the aggregation ran over five cohorts instead of six and the estimand changed inside the bootstrap. Equivalence within a quarter of an ordinal step consequently holds for five of the eight outcomes instead of four, and the ratio of restricted to full-sample standard errors becomes 1.44-2.67 (median 2.48) instead of 1.73-3.63 (median 2.44). The version also adds a bootstrap audit, a complete-separation diagnostic for the affected cohort including a directly programmed group-time parameter, and an empirical benchmark for the equivalence margins; records the membership of the two subsets of 34 countries in Supplementary Table 3; corrects the internal title of Figure 5, which asserted an attribution the comparison between samples cannot establish; and ships the execution logs of the pipeline.   Version 1.0.2 (2026-10-21) incorporates the second and third review rounds: lag-informed treatment dating; date-shift sensitivity extended to one through six years; a manuscript consistency audit; correction of the specification space from 75 rows to 60 distinct configurations by removing 15 duplicate configurations; and equivalence tests for the support-restricted subsample (Supplementary Table 9). Corresponding reference tables, figures, supplementary material, and verification checks are updated.   Validation for this archive: the complete pipeline was rerun from the raw sources on 2026-10-23 and its logs are included in outputs/logs/; the verification script passed 107 of 107 checks, 54 on values reported in the manuscript and 53 comparing every regenerated result table with the archived reference; all 131 entries in the SHA-256 manifest were verified.   Code is licensed under MIT. Derived tables, figures, and supplementary material are licensed under CC BY 4.0; third-party data terms are documented in LICENSE-DATA.md. Digital Society Project and V-Dem source files and derived analytical panels are not redistributed; download instructions are included.

summary: The package contains all the data and scripts used to produce the results presented in the paper "AST-SZZ: an SZZ Algorithm with AST Change Clustering and Backporting". Datasets A dataset is a list of scenarios, each of which contains the name of a GitHub repository, a bug-fixing commit hash, and one or more bug-inducing commit hashes. The datasets are summarized in the following table. Name Source File ( datasets/* ) Repository root Scenarios DS_GITHUB-j Rosa et al. DS_GITHUB-j74.json github-j74 74 DS_APACHE Wen et al. DS_APACHE236.json apache236 236 DS_RECENT Original DS_RECENT38.json recent38 38 Note that some repositories are no longer accessible, and some bug-fixing commits do not modify source code. We have excluded the corresponding scenarios from the dataset. Preparation Download the following. astszz-amd64.tar.xz (for x64) or astszz-arm64.tar.xz  (for arm64) github-j74.tar.xz apache236.tar.xz recent38.tar.xz github-j74-no-mesg.tar.xz (rewritten to remove the commit messages) apache236-no-mesg.tar.xz (rewritten to remove the commit messages) recent38-no-mesg.tar.xz (rewritten to remove the commit messages) llm4szz.tar.xz  (for the LLM4SZZ experiments only) agentszz.tar.xz  (for the AgentSZZ experiments only) agents-for-szz.tar.xz  (for the Simple-SZZ-Agent experiments only) pyszz_v2.tar.xz  (for the pyszz_v2 experiments only) RESULTS.tar.xz  (the results of the experiments) Then import the image appropriate for your host's architecture. docker import astszz-amd64.tar.xz \     --change "WORKDIR /root" \     --change "CMD [\"/usr/bin/bash\"]" \     astszz Use astszz-arm64.tar.xz instead if your architecture is arm64. The images are built from the codinuum/cca:base image on Docker Hub. AST-SZZ is implemented using Diff/AST , CCA , and modified versions of DDJ and D3J . Finally, start a container and then extract the repositories. docker run -ti -v ${PWD}:/mnt/work --name astszz astszz tar Jxf /mnt/work/github-j74.tar.xz tar Jxf /mnt/work/apache236.tar.xz tar Jxf /mnt/work/recent38.tar.xz Alternatively, you can clone the repositories from GitHub. scripts/clone_repos.py datasets/DS_GITHUB-j74.json github-j74 scripts/clone_repos.py datasets/DS_APACHE236.json apache236 scripts/clone_repos.py datasets/DS_RECENT38.json recent38 Replication AST-SZZ Since the replication is time-consuming, we recommend running the experiments on only a randomly sampled subset of <N> scenarios using the --nsamples <N> option. The following command starts the replication run, where <N_PROCS>  specifies the maximum number of processes to use. scripts/test_astszz.py -u -r -p <N_PROCS> [--nsamples <N>] \     <DATASET_JSON> <REPO_ROOT> For example, the following command runs the script using at most four processes on a sample of three scenarios from DS_RECENT. scripts/test_astszz.py -u -r -p 4 --nsamples 3 \     datasets/DS_RECENT38.json recent38 To disable change clustering, remove the -u (untangling) and -r (remove refactoring) options from the command line. Note that removing both options also disables multiprocessing, since one process is assigned to each sub-SZZ instance operating on a variant derived from a change cluster. To disable the additional conflict rules, add the --orig-d3j  option. The script stores an intermediate result in the  LOG directory. To generate the final result from the intermediate result, use the postprocess_astszz.py  script. scripts/postprocess_astszz.py \     LOG/intermediate.DS_{GITHUB-j74|APACHE236|RECENT38}.json You can also run test_astszz.py on a single scenario using the --sid  option. mv LOG LOG0 scripts/test_astszz.py -u -r -p 4 --sid 5 \     datasets/DS_RECENT38.json recent38 LLM-based SZZs Running all LLM-based experiments requires substantial time and incurs substantial costs (several hundred US dollars). Name Paper Directory LLM4SZZ Tang et al.

summary: Version 2.0, October 24, 2026: Empirical Revision Substantially revised Paper I to incorporate exploratory geochemical validation using published EarthChem and Alcott et al. (2026) measurements. Added EBA-1/EBA-2 sulfur-isotope change-point analysis, independent phosphorus and redox comparisons, alternative-boundary null testing, and blocked predictive model comparisons. The core source–sink hypothesis is retained, while claims concerning a uniquely identified tipping point, regional diachrony, and demonstrated feedback causation are explicitly qualified. The revision includes updated literature context, methodological limitations, and supplementary analytical materials. Supersedes version 1.0 as the current research statement while preserving the original publication history. The Great Oxidation Event (GOE) reflects the evolving balance between biological oxygen production, reductant consumption, atmospheric photochemistry, and ocean–sediment exchange. This paper develops a basin-resolved source–sink threshold framework in which regional oxygenation responses may differ despite shared atmospheric forcing. Version 2.0 extends the original theoretical framework through exploratory quantitative analysis of published EBA-1 and EBA-2 drill-core geochemistry, including sulfur mass-independent fractionation, phosphorus distributions, organic carbon, and redox-sensitive trace elements. An exploratory sulfur-isotope change point was identified at 1,336.87 m in EBA-2. Independent geochemical measurements exhibit substantial variation across this interval. However, depth-controlled null comparisons and blocked out-of-sample prediction do not establish a uniquely coordinated tipping-point transition. Predictive improvements are restricted to selected indicators and depend partly on baseline specification. These findings preserve the source–sink feedback framework as a testable explanation for nonlinear and spatially heterogeneous oxygenation while distinguishing theoretical plausibility from demonstrated causal dynamics. The revised manuscript provides empirical comparisons, competing-model evaluations, explicit limitations, and falsification criteria for future research. Part of the Planetary Convexity Series, Paper I.
title: Diachronous Oxygenation as a Planetary Tipping Point

summary: This dataset is the supplementary material for the manuscript "Decision Neutrality of Forecast Revisions in Microgrids with Photovoltaics and Battery Storage" by Yun Xing (Hohai University), submitted to Applied Sciences (MDPI). Version 1.0, 25 October 2026. Overview The study asks when adopting a revised next-day forecast changes a battery dispatch decision, rather than only the predicted cost. It derives two checkable sufficient reset conditions under which old and revised forecasts produce next-day storage value functions that differ only by an additive constant. A fixed-input perturbation bound separates this local neutrality from realized rolling-policy performance. Five policies (FF, FS, SF, SS and DAY) are compared on 522 community-days from 270 measured households aggregated into nine synthetic communities, with three synthetic tariffs and two import regimes. Key results - Freezing next-day forecasts is numerically neutral under unlimited imports across the tested tariffs. - Under a 30 kW import cap and time-of-use pricing, retaining midnight targets (DAY) lowers total operating cost by 3.105% relative to full updating (FF). Lower unmet-demand penalties account for 88.3% of the reduction; the import-bill reduction is 0.588%. - Freezing both forecasts while replanning (SS) costs 0.054% more than FF under the same six-hour replanning schedule, separating forecast adoption from target retention. - Under the same cap and tariff, freezing only the next-day forecast (FS) costs 0.188% more than FF. - Matched-calendar comparisons show that the magnitude of update effects depends on the controller scheme. Contents 1. Supporting_Results_and_Protocol.zip: verified reproducibility archive with 3,833 files, including fixed protocols, derived community inputs, customer-community mapping, analysis code, result tables, 15,660 policy-day records, 9,396 local terminal comparisons, 1,496 matched-calendar controller records, half-hour trajectories, figures and an internal manifest. 2. Supplementary_Guide.pdf: Supplementary Methods S1 and S2, extended uncertainty tables S1-S6, data dictionary notes and the run sequence. 3. README_ZENODO.txt: contents, usage order and scope notes. 4. LICENSE.txt: licensing note for code and derived data. 5. CITATION.cff: citation metadata. 6. zenodo_metadata.json: suggested metadata for this record. 7. SHA256SUMS.txt: SHA-256 checksums of the files in this archive. Reproduction Verify the files against SHA256SUMS.txt, extract Supporting_Results_and_Protocol.zip, and read README.txt, RUN_REPRODUCTION.txt and DATA_DICTIONARY.md before running anything. The recorded environment is Python 3.13.9 with NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.16.3, pandas 2.3.3, Matplotlib 3.10.6 and openpyxl 3.1.5. Entry points cover the primary experiment, aggregation, availability sensitivity, diagnostics, both controller families, benchmarks and independent checks. The archive also supports a fresh single-group replay and a full audit without the author's original workspace. Data provenance and scope The household data are the Ausgrid 2012-2013 Solar Home Electricity Data, version 2, obtained from data.gov.au and the BetterGrids mirror. Raw provider records are not redistributed; provider URLs, version and SHA-256 are recorded in RUN_REPRODUCTION.txt and raw_source_manifest.json. Derived community inputs, results and trajectories are included. The archived results are the recorded reference outputs, not new observations. Communities, tariffs and batteries are synthetic scenario inputs, and the manuscript states the limits of the evidence. License Unless otherwise stated, the code and derived data in this package are provided under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0). The original household data are not redistributed and remain subject to the provider terms. Related manuscript Submitted to Applied Sciences (MDPI). The manuscript DOI will be added to this record after publication. Contact Yun Xing, College of Com
title: Decision Neutrality of Forecast Revisions in Microgrids with Photovoltaics and Battery Storage - Supplementary Material

summary: International observation systems reveal a consequential possibility: scientific information can be generated, validated, and circulated across institutional and political boundaries without requiring a single authority over all observations or a uniform distribution of capacities . Yet the existence of data-sharing protocols does not by itself establish shared understanding, mutual trust, legitimate reuse, or equitable participation in the production of knowledge . This discussion paper investigates the technical, epistemic, and institutional conditions under which global observation and knowledge infrastructures might be constructed and sustained . Drawing on meteorological and oceanographic cooperation, it distinguishes observational coverage, data availability, interoperability, interpretation, and collective authority. It proposes a preliminary federated research architecture connecting situated observation nodes, provenance and quality records, semantic and model translation, distributed computation, access governance, correction, and contestation. It treats mathematical, physical, social, and normative languages as historically formed manifestations and practices within generative-relational systems, distinguishing their conditional formal invariance from claims to universally identical representation. It further investigates why actors situated in different generative and institutional histories may interpret shared evidence differently, and proposes a bounded research vocabulary for mutually workable norms, continued disagreement, and rule revision without assuming epistemic consensus. The paper conceptualizes trust as a historically constituted relation supported in part by verifiable commitments, reciprocal inquiry, accountable institutions, and effective remedy rather than as a property supplied by cryptography or open data alone. It further specifies prospective services for common knowledge creation and circulation, generalized translation of heterogeneous generative-relational contexts, and traceable transformations of distinct forms of value. A staged validation design differentiates synthetic policy gates, cross-node scientific comparison, productive-capacity trials, and site-dependent ecological and institutional review. A cross-layer assessment profile separates technical interchange, scientific warrant, claimed competent authority, and effective contestation, without deriving legal or ethical legitimacy from technical success. It also examines epistemic and infrastructural asymmetries, the sensitivity of ecological and community data, the incompleteness of model-based assimilation, and the risks of concentrating interpretive authority in highly capable AI systems. Global weather and ocean observation provide instructive but bounded cases, not evidence that all knowledge should be made public or placed under centralized control. The proposed programme remains exploratory and separates conceptual architecture from implemented infrastructure, independent empirical assessment, and normative justification.
title: Global Observation and Knowledge Infrastructures: A Study of Collective Inquiry across Heterogeneous Relational Systems

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-five entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.
title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

summary: Replication package for the article "Facts versus Claims: Provenance-Grounded Defense for LLM Security Analysts under Adaptive Evidence-Substrate Injection". Contents: the analysis notebooks in run order, the skeletonization and evidence-view modules, the frozen configuration files (closed vocabulary, normalization, provenance flags and their thresholds, triage instruction, framing notes, output schema, decoding parameters, sampling rule and attack payloads), the figure generator, and the per-request result records in Parquet that support every table and figure in the article. The analysts are two quantized 8B models served locally over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4 and Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ. Decoding is deterministic (temperature 0.0, top_p 1.0, max_tokens 256, seed 42) with a guided JSON schema, and every call is cached by sha1(model + prompt), so the reported numbers are reproducible from the cache without a GPU. The underlying request corpus is CSIC 2010, which is publicly available and is not redistributed here except as derived per-request records.
title: Replication package for "Facts versus Claims: Provenance-Grounded Defense for LLM Security Analysts under Adaptive Evidence-Substrate Injection"

The deposited materials include model validation results at hourly and daily temporal scales, summary performance metrics, variable definitions, and documentation of the processing workflow. The dataset supports the station-based model evaluation described in the associated research. It does not, by itself, constitute the complete gridded dataset for the 1991–2025 regional reconstruction. summary: The work builds a foundation of physics from a single assumption: everything is a process, and a process is an ideal sine; its centre, the balance, is the observer. Only the square — intensity without phase — passes between levels; from this arise dimensions, the arrow of time, the quantum and the standard. On this basis stable particles are built as standing waves together with their galactic analogues, the initial rules of quantum mechanics and relativity are derived, and the constants are linked to a single number — the speed of light. Agreement with experiment is at the level of a few percent; the model attributes the discrepancies to the imperfection of the standard. Main results The four stable particles (neutrino, electron, neutron, proton) are the four stable states of a standing wave; masses from the speed of light alone: electron +0.7 %, nucleons about −3 % [result given hypotheses]. The Born rule, the randomness of a single outcome, the 2√2 limit in the Bell test, spin ½ and g = 2 [result]. The Lorentz transformation from the “speed budget” c² = v² + v_int², the Klein — Gordon and Schrödinger equations, Schwarzschild gravitational time dilation and the light deflection of 1.75″ [result]. Similarity of the small and the large with the step c⁴: the image of the neutron is the stellar mass of the Milky Way (5.5·10¹⁰ versus (6.1 ± 1.1)·10¹⁰ solar masses) [hypothesis, numerical agreement]. The large end is built by the same logic as the microworld: the construction yields the Hubble constant H₀ = 1/(5c²) ≈ 68.7 km/s/Mpc and the smallest acceleration of galaxies a₀ = 1/(10πc) [result given hypotheses]. The gravitational constant G ≈ c^(−6/5) (0.8 %); the mass of the Universe and the scale of dark energy are expressed through c [hypothesis]. The fine-structure constant has been found as the number 1/α ≈ 4·(c/2π)^(1/5) (0.22 %); its meaning is open [observation]. Limitations: the accuracy is percent-level, not parts per million; the standard and several constants remain open questions. The status of each statement is given in the text. Revision dated 2026-10-24:   Version 24.2 continues to unwind the process from the large end (Part VI). The qualitative descriptions have been refined: the black hole is the centre of mass of the whole construction of a galaxy, and its mass is mainly dark matter; the process itself is not entirely hidden — we see its manifestation in dark matter and spin. The quantum of the large end is described as the passage of the spin through the point of balance, where zero and the limit are one and the same; the flat rotation curve as one and the same energy level at every radius of the disc. The birth of baryons is described: the rotation and acceleration of dark matter, the limit of tempo 1/c, the constant birth of particles in a galaxy. A qualitative explanation has been found of why the fractal transfer of the parameters of the neutron gives a link precisely with the stellar mass of the Milky Way. A qualitative explanation of coupling at another level is given: in a galaxy two different processes of mass formation — dark matter and baryons — are linked in space by rotation, not in the dimension of mass, so here the coupling is visible, whereas in the neutron it is hidden beyond mass. The abstract, the summary of Part VI and the register have been brought into agreement; the changes are made in all three languages.         Работа строит основу физики из одного допущения: всё — процесс, а процесс — идеальный синус; его центр, баланс, — наблюдатель. Между уровнями проходит только квадрат — интенсивность без фазы; отсюда рождаются измерения, стрела времени, квант и эталон. На этой основе построены стабильные частицы как стоячие волны и их галактические аналоги, выведены исходные
title: The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton

summary: This deposit is the numerical companion to “One-Sided p-Explicit Stability for High-Order Cut Finite Element Nitsche Methods” by Erik Burman, Peter Hansbo, Mats G. Larson and Karl Larsson. It contains Python experiment code, case parameters, compact reference data, reproducibility instructions and the Numerical Verification Guide. The implementation uses two-dimensional triangular P p finite elements and CPU-based dense linear algebra. The studies cover polynomial continuation, one-sided flux estimates, penalty thresholds, convergence, numerical precision, Schwarz comparisons and exact tube certificates. The compact data retain 4,959 reference observations, 239 failed criteria and 22 tables, including known accuracy flags, the original solver-stopping failure and unresolved higher-degree attempts. Selected validation covers 15 numerical commands across ten study families; it is not a rerun of the full 257-command campaign or an audit of the omitted raw archives. Raw run archives and manuscript sources are not included. Detailed run records and exact certificates can be regenerated using the documented commands. The continuation and tube studies are tested on Apple Silicon macOS and Linux x86-64. The remaining supplied validation studies require the documented Linux configuration with a 64-bit longdouble significand and multiprocessing fork. The package includes file-integrity checks and pinned dependencies. Licensing is component-specific: Python code and software documentation are licensed under MIT; numerical data and the Numerical Verification Guide are licensed under CC BY 4.0. See LICENSE for the precise scope. AI assistance and author responsibility are disclosed in README.md. This documentation update aligns the guide’s references with the revised manuscript numbering. Numerical code, case inputs, reference data and dependency pins are unchanged; numerical tests were not rerun for this update. Source repository: KarlLarssonUmU/one-sided-hp-cutfem Archived commit: bae06c644b21f723ee636ed67663c99e06004cfd .
title: Numerical Companion to One-Sided p-Explicit Stability for High-Order Cut Finite Element Nitsche Methods

summary: The relentless pursuit of modeling quantum many-body systems has exposed a profound epistemic and technological schism in modern physics. As the dimension of the Hilbert space expands exponentially with each additional particle, direct computational modeling via classical state vectors becomes a physical impossibility. Concurrently, the physical realization of fault-tolerant Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) is stymied by persistent decoherence, fragile topological phases, and exorbitant error correction overheads. In response to this paradigm, a disparate array of mathematical techniques and classical computational heuristics have emerged, often mis-categorized under the broad, imprecise umbrella of "quantum computing" or "quantum simulation." This exhaustive report serves as the formal proposal and rigorous justification for the establishment of a new, distinct scientific discipline: Quantum Mathematics and Quantum Emulation. By synthesizing avant-garde mathematical constructs—including non-commutative geometry, von Neumann operator algebras, and the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra of renormalization—with High-Performance Computing (HPC) techniques such as the Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) and Projected Entangled Pair States (PEPS), this field systematically truncates quantum state spaces for deterministic emulation. Architected by Syed Abraham Ahmed, Founder and CEO of Lifeline AI, this document serves as the synergetic collection of prior art and modern innovation to  create the field of Quantum Mathematics and Quantum Emulation . This document formally synthesizes these isolated mathematical and computational breakthroughs into a unified discipline by acknowledging the foundational prior art, in the noble pursuit of scientific integrity, accuracy, and logical justification. It is fundamentally necessary to correctly re-categorize these algorithmic efforts away from quantum hardware simulation and unify rooting them in rigorous mathematical compression—ensuring continued scientific merit and progress for distinguishing the accurate categorization of research funding mechanisms. Furthermore, the development of the novel field of Quantum Mathematics provides an actionable and definitive pathway to empower the future of scientific discovery, utilizing existing supercomputing constructs to bypass the limitations of physical quantum hardware, and champion the synergistic fusion of these existing elements to unlock entirely novel computational paradigms. Part 1 establishes the historical and taxonomic necessity of this classification, while Part 2 details the rigorous sub-Planckian algebraic architectures required for its execution. Ultimately, by rooting the existing siloed unification of Quantum Mathematics away from the physical Quantum hardware simulation, this structural re-categorization is a fundamental necessity for both scientific integrity and provides the computational pathway to bypass hardware limitations and compute the quantum realm using existing supercomputing powerhouse constructs.
title: The Creation of Quantum Mathematics and Quantum Emulation

summary: Water scarcity is becoming a growing problem worldwide due to the expansion of industry, population growth and climate change, and the need for clean and potable water is becoming increasingly important. Traditional wastewater treatment techniques such as sedimentation, filtration, and chlorination often fail to remove emerging contaminants (ECs), such as pharmaceuticals, microplastics, heavy metals, and sometimes create toxic byproducts. Thus, nanotechnology has come up as a novel solution with materials of incredible surface area, tunable reactivity and adsorption capacities. In recent years, a paradigm change towards sustainability has led to the creation of "green" or biogenic nanomaterials. The green nanomaterials are synthesized from renewable biological resources like plant extracts and microbial consortia, which reduce environmental footprints, the use of hazardous chemicals and provide cost-effective remediation. The present review covers all the recent developments in the use of green nanomaterials such as metal/metal oxide nanoparticles (Ag, TiO₂, Fe₃O₄, ZnO), carbon-based nanostructures and bio-inspired nanocomposites in wastewater monitoring and remediation. Systematically, the main mechanisms of contaminant removal, such as physical adsorption, chemical adsorption, photocatalytic degradation, electrochemical reduction and advanced membrane filtration are explored. In addition, the incorporation of very sensitive nanosensors for real-time environmental monitoring is discussed. Recent computational methods, such as Molecular Dynamics (MD), Density Functional Theory (DFT), and Machine Learning (ML), are emphasized as key tools to translate experimental design into application, and to predict the efficacy and toxicity of nanoparticles. Finally, this review critically examines the issues of scalability, economic viability and nanotoxicity, and outlines the path for sustainable implementation of nanotechnology in water management on a global scale. Graphical Abstract: Comprehensive framework for green nanomaterials in wastewater treatment, illustrating synthesis pathways from biological sources, removal mechanisms, and a critical overview of benefits, limitations, and future applications. title: Sustainable Innovations in Green Nanomaterials for Contaminated Water Management and Remediation

summary: Resilience and Recovery in a \mathbb{Z}_5-Graded NonAssociative System: A Computational Study of Constraint Disruption and Re-Stabilization C. J. Tully, Independent Researcher Engineer, Australia   https://orcid.org/0009 - 0007 - 5661 - 7332 chloetully5@gmail.com   25 th October 2026 Abstract We present a particle-based simulator whose interaction rule on a five-dimensional sector is given by a non-associative, \mathbb{Z}_5-graded multiplication table with golden-ratio weights. The system is subject to spatial forces under several model choices and is equipped with hard gates (velocity clipping and minimum-distance floors). We define a coherence metric on the graded sector and an associator norm that quantifies local failure of associativity. In a controlled perturbation experiment, a sudden shock applied to half the particles at step 75 produces an immediate drop in coherence (0.968 \to 0.511) and a sharp rise in the associator norm (0.008 \to 0.108). The associator continues to rise for approximately ten steps after the external shock has ended, reaching a peak of 0.224, after which both quantities relax: by step 149 coherence has recovered to 0.885   the associator has returned to 0.013. The result demonstrates that, under the chosen force law and hard gates, the graded interaction is capable of re-establishing lowassociator, high-coherence configurations after a severe disruption. We discuss the finding in relation to organizational closure, path dependence, and the distinction between structural and dynamical aspects of self-maintenance. Keywords: Graded algebras, non-associativity, organizational closure, resilience, path dependence, computational models, TT-G41

summary: This candidate extends the LWS research bench with three computational modules. The sequential-context module preserves the protocol and reference outcomes of the five-intersection experiment. The functional-alignment module compares equal feature budgets on already inspected outcomes. The branching module is a development pilot with short movement-specific lanes and a strong lane-aware scalar baseline. Development analyses are not presented as new confirmatory experiments. The package includes fixed protocols, generators, feature inputs, readable model parameters, reference predictions, complete comparison tables and tests. The original public v7 ZIP is included unchanged. New entry points separate integrity checks, cached model refits, engineering simulations and full raw regeneration. Runtime paths are resolved within the extracted package or an explicitly selected work directory. Python dependencies and SUMO must be installed separately at the recorded versions. The candidate was tested from a fresh extraction on Windows with the existing pinned scientific environment. All 17 tests passed. Refitting 54 fixed model variants reproduced all 51,642 saved probabilities with a maximum numerical difference of zero. Ten engineering simulations were regenerated and matched the reference canonical observations and feature rows. Reads from the original study directories were blocked during the checks. These checks establish reproducibility within the tested environment, not new scientific confirmation. Full regeneration of all 494 historical simulations was not performed in this candidate validation. It is available as a separate explicit command. Installation of dependencies on a clean machine and execution on other operating systems have not been tested. The 30 m sequential outcome and the 15 m branching outcome remain separate. No general predictive superiority of functional token boundaries is claimed. Own code is licensed under MIT. Own synthetic results and documentation are licensed under CC BY 4.0. The package excludes manuscripts, expert assessments, consents, signatures, third-party raw trajectories, videos and simulator binaries. The original v7 archive retains its own metadata and licenses. Developed in institutional competitive project STN-AI, no. 210318, funded by the European Union, NextGenerationEU. Data source: pNEUMA – open-traffic.epfl.ch.

summary: Modern physics achieves extraordinary predictive precision, and it has been taught that the strange picture attached to its equations is what nature is: a wave that is a wave of nothing, a particle that is nowhere until observed, action at a distance with no carrier, fields with no medium. That picture was not discovered. It was adopted because the equations worked, and the equations themselves say nothing about it. This framework holds that the equations describe something physical, and sets out to say what: space is a physical medium with material properties, matter consists of structures within it, and the phenomena of the quantum, electromagnetic, relativistic and cosmological domains follow mechanically from that one premise. The quantum part has now been simulated: a definite particle moving through such a medium, guided by its own wave, produces the double-slit interference pattern (Atallah 2026). What this framework explains where current physics offers only the formalism: Quantum mechanics: Double-slit interference, measurement effects, and wave-particle duality emerge from compression waves in spatial medium interacting with definite particle structures; the entanglement correlations, which exceed Bell's bound, remain an open problem for the framework (Section 2). A particle's acceleration disturbs the medium; the disturbance disperses, and the part whose group velocity matches the particle's speed travels with it, with a wavelength set by the particle's momentum through the medium's dispersion—higher momentum, shorter wavelength. When approaching a barrier with slits, the bow wave reaches the slits first (several wavelengths ahead of the particle), diffracts through both openings, and creates an interference pattern before the particle arrives. The particle passes through one slit; beyond the slits its wave has fanned into lanes of constructive interference, and the particle, taking its direction from the wave's flow, follows a lane to the screen. Particles land on the bright bands. The interference pattern follows sinc-squared envelope (from rectangular slit geometry via Fourier transform) multiplied by cosine-squared fringes (from two-source interference)—pure wave mechanics in spatial medium. This single mechanism explains why slow electrons create wide patterns while fast electrons create narrow patterns, why red light diffracts differently than blue light, and why the relationship follows λ = h/p for all particles. No wave function collapse, no particles “being waves,” no action at a distance, no ontological uncertainty—just definite particles creating momentum-dependent compression waves in a physical medium, with each particle independently steered by its own wave's interference pattern. This mechanism has been simulated in a particle medium with no constant fitted to the pattern: one disturbance at launch, a silent coast, and a single rule for direction reproduce the two-slit pattern of the wave itself, its scaling with wavelength, and its disappearance when one slit is closed (Atallah 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23570390). Electromagnetism: All phenomena from DC through optical frequencies emerge from two particle types in spatial medium. Teslons (field mediators with orientation and rotation degrees of freedom) create static electric and magnetic fields. Photons (propagating structures) carry current in conductors and electromagnetic energy in free space. This unified mechanism explains transmission lines, inductors, capacitors, the photoelectric effect, antennas, the right-hand rule, and the Meissner effect—all from spatial medium mechanics through photon-teslon-photon conversion processes. Cosmology: Hubble redshift, supernova time stretching, and CMB uniformity result from photon energy loss and propagation delays through spatial medium over cosmological distances. No Big Bang, no cosmic inflation, no dark energy required. Galaxy rotation curves result from extend
title: Universal Mechanics: A Unified Physics Framework

summary: We study a deterministic comparison of material composition across a fixed time cut when entire contexts have uncertain dates constrained by intervals and a stratigraphic partial order. Source-specific recovery ratios are shared by all contexts and both periods and range over a compact positive rational polytope. Feasible period allocations are exactly the lower ideals satisfying explicit forced assignments. The sign of composition change reduces to a linear weight on these ideals. With the recovery vertices supplied explicitly, all admissible explanations can therefore be checked by polynomially many minimum-cut computations, with constructive dates and recovery witnesses. Sharp finite odds-ratio bounds admit exact enumeration over allocations and recovery vertices. Computing their lower endpoint is nevertheless NP-hard: the associated decision problem is NP-complete in an anchored two-source subclass with known recovery and no stratigraphic relations, even though every allocation has the same positive sign. We also give exact domain and attainment rules for zero masses and open recovery faces. The distinction concerns this shared-mechanism model; the closure, fractional-programming and complexity tools used in its analysis are classical.
title: Direction and magnitude of composition change under shared recovery and uncertain context dates

summary: We study cumulative non-surface heat loss in a rectangular heat model with known forcing and mixed boundary data. The unknown initial perturbation belongs to one fixed spectral H2 ball, and finitely many physical temperature readings have a prescribed joint ellipsoidal error. Standard optimal recovery theory gives the sharp global scalar error. We make this result explicit for the cumulative heat functional, retaining all three-dimensional observation modes and constructing worst initial states. Algebraic and exponential spectral tails give convergent certificates for the infinite-dimensional problem. The unique old worst state yields a necessary and sufficient condition for a new reading to reduce the error, including correlated deterministic errors, together with a positive lower bound on the reduction. For a 100 m column with fixed norm length 25 m and no prior readings, we prove an analytic short-time separation: at the same time and error tolerance, one reading at 75 m strictly reduces the cumulative-heat error while a surface reading leaves it unchanged. A computable sufficient time interval accompanies this result. The radius, reference field, forcing, boundary data and joint error set are inputs; their physical calibration is a separate problem.
title: Cumulative boundary heat from finite temperature readings: sharp deterministic recovery and a short-time depth separation

summary: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence in agriculture has improved the production of crops, monitoring of the overall process of farming, resource management, and what type of resources will be used for more and better production of the crops in today's era. Transparency-like, if the crops got damages, then the farmers have clear and accurate knowledge about the failure of the crop. Explainable Artificial Intelligence addresses this challenge by providing clear, interpretable insights into how the AI system makes decisions. This paper explores how AI is beneficial in farming, focusing on several techniques such as feature importance, visualization, and rule-based explanations that improve decision-making in crop management. This also explores several tools-like, the weather condition, equipment required that gives more than expected outcome, and much more. By this study, some of the features I want to add through technology which helps farmers for better production. The addition of technology in farming enhances transparency, trust, and sustainability in modern farming practices. The importance of XAI in agriculture forms the foundation of this research paper, which intends to present various explanation techniques and study how they will lead to trustworthy decision-making in crop management. This study also presents the use of technological tools such as climate monitoring systems, automated equipment, soil sensors, and data-driven forecasting models that work in harmony with XAI for delivering superior results. XAI provides clear and understandable explanations-such that farmers would not only use the AI-based tool but fully trust and utilize it to truly make farming smarter and more resilient.

summary: We study full-cohort change in two binary latent states observed through a shared, incompletely calibrated anchor and a second item whose channel may change between waves. All baseline items are observed; follow-up response depends only on the follow-up latent state, with a bounded selection odds ratio. The input is the entire twenty-cell observed law. A nonzero respondent cross-wave anchor covariance gives point identification through classical three-view and shadow-variable mechanisms. At zero covariance the latent transition has rank one. We eliminate the drifting channels, obtain the exact feasible rectangle for the common anchor, and show that one corner realizes the complete set of possible signs of latent change. This yields an explicit sharp selection threshold. A positive-probability example has identical observed laws and opposite changes; full-rank perturbations approach this law while retaining a fixed target gap. The results are conditional population-law calculations with external calibration inputs.
title: Sharp directions of change at a rank boundary in a two-wave binary measurement model

summary: Text-to-speech (TTS) technology has significantly transformed human-machine interactions, facilitating seamless communication between humans and computers. However, achieving high-quality TTS remains a significant challenge, especially in synthesizing natural and nuanced speech. In this study, we investigate the potential of HiFiGAN-Hubert-Soft (HHS) vocoders to enhance the performance of TTS models, with a focus on integrating the HHS vocoder into the Voicebox TTS model—a versatile and scalable TTS system developed by Meta AI. Through both subjective (mean opinion score) and objective (speech similarity and visualization metric) evaluations, we illustrate that the HHS vocoder significantly enhances the naturalness and nuance of synthesized speech compared to the baseline HiFiGAN vocoder. This improvement is particularly pronounced in cases where pronunciation variations are minor or context-dependent. Our findings emphasize the potential of HHS vocoders in elevating TTS performance and laying the foundation for further advancements in TTS technology.
title: Improving Speech Naturalness and Nuance using HiFiGAN-Hubert-Soft Vocoder: A Case Study of the Voicebox TTS Model
